Title: Compute every figure live from stored rows, with the required indexes and no rollup
Description: Nothing in this system runs on a schedule, so nothing is precomputed: no rollup table, no materialised view, no nightly summary, no cached report and no background warm-up. A cached report is a stale report a manager will act on.
AcceptanceCriteria: rg -n 'MATERIALIZED VIEW|rollup|report_cache' backend/migrations backend/app returns 0 hits and SELECT count(*) FROM pg_matviews returns 0; after a dashboard request the only Redis key created is the rate-limit bucket key for that user, asserted by diffing SCAN over the whole keyspace before and after, and no key in the keyspace holds a value containing the substring takings_paise - two identical GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 requests separated by one captured booking of 1 Standard seat at 25000 paise return takings_paise differing by exactly 25000; after the Alembic history is applied, SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes contains an index on each of showtime(starts_at), showtime(screen_id, starts_at), booking(showtime_id), booking_seat(booking_id), booking(payment_id) and payment(state); the payment join is written payment.id = booking.payment_id, asserted by rg -n 'payment\.booking_id' backend/app backend/migrations returning 0 hits and by SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='payment' AND column_name='booking_id' returning 0, the column not existing; rg -n 'metrics' backend/app/api/reports backend/app/domain/reports returns 0 hits, so no figure on this surface is read from /metrics; and rg -n 'app\.domain\.reports|app\.api\.reports' backend/app/domain/booking returns 0 hits, so no reporting work is performed inside the booking confirmation transaction
SourceRef: P-RPT-12 E7 S4 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-057 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 SRC-002 §5.4.1

Title: Rate-limit the reports router per user, and fail closed when Redis is unreachable
Description: One per-user token bucket named REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE with a starting value of 60, an estimate to be tuned once measured. No per-IP bucket, because every caller here is authenticated and a per-IP bucket would put twelve managers in one building into one bucket.
AcceptanceCriteria: REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE is validated at boot as a positive integer and the application exits non-zero with a message containing that variable name when it is absent, empty or non-numeric, asserted on all three inputs; with it set to 60, the 61st GET /api/reports/dashboard from one user inside a 60 second window returns 429 with code RATE_LIMITED, a Retry-After header of exactly 1, and the message 'Too many requests. Try again in 1 second.' in the singular; the wait is computed at render time as ceil(window_seconds / capacity) = ceil(60/60) = 1, proved by serving Retry-After 2 to the same screen and seeing it render 'Too many requests. Try again in 2 seconds.' in the plural, and rg -n '30 seconds' frontend/src/features/reports returns 0 hits; a second user's first request inside that same window returns 200, proving the bucket is per user, and rg -n 'remote_addr|X-Forwarded-For|client\.host' backend/app/api/reports returns 0 hits, no per-IP bucket existing; the bucket is shared across EP-RPT-01, EP-RPT-02, EP-RPT-03 and EP-RPT-04, verified by exhausting it on /api/reports/dashboard and getting 429 on the next /api/reports/scope; with Redis stopped every /api/reports/ endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with 'The dashboard cannot be loaded right now. A service it depends on is unreachable.' and never a 200; and this setting has exactly one name and one home, asserted by rg -c 'REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE' backend/app returning 1, that one hit being the settings declaration and every other site reading it through the settings object rather than restating the name, and by rg -no 'REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT[A-Za-z_]*' backend/app 'docs/03 PRD/sections/E8_crosscutting.md' - the file that carries both the cross-cutting rate-limit table and the configuration inventory - yielding exactly one distinct variable name, so no near-miss spelling of this setting exists in the code or in either table
SourceRef: P-RPT-12 E7 S4 FR-ADR-028 FR-ADR-058 SRC-002 §7.1

Title: Build the dashboard's opening load, scope line and hall filter
Description: The screen opens on period=day with date omitted and issues three requests, not one: EP-RPT-03 and EP-RPT-01 together on mount, EP-RPT-02 after EP-RPT-01 returns. Hall names live on EP-RPT-03 alone, because EP-RPT-01's screen_ids is an array of integers. The out-of-service hall rule is P-ADM-16's, applied here and not restated.
AcceptanceCriteria: On mounting /dashboard the screen issues exactly two requests in parallel - GET /api/reports/scope and GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day with no date parameter present in the recorded URL - and issues GET /api/reports/showtimes?period=day&limit=50&offset=0 only after the dashboard request resolves, asserted in a component test with a mocked fetch that records call order and resolution timing; the Day tab carries aria-selected true on arrival and exactly one period tab carries aria-selected true at all times, asserted after each of the three tab activations; date is omitted rather than computed on the client, and rg -n 'getTimezoneOffset|toISOString|Date\.now\(' frontend/src/features/reports/dashboard returns 0 hits; the scope line renders the exact string 'Halls shown: Hall 3, Hall 5.' for manager M by looking each id of EP-RPT-01's screen_ids up in EP-RPT-03's screens array in screen_id ascending order, and the string 'Halls shown: 3, 5.' does not appear anywhere in the rendered DOM; for an administrator it renders 'Halls shown: every hall.'; applying &screen_id=3 changes the line to 'Halls shown: Hall 3.' while the hall filter still offers both options; the hall filter's first option's rendered text is 'All my halls' for a manager and 'All halls' for an administrator and selecting it produces a request URL with no screen_id parameter, the remaining options are EP-RPT-03's screens in screen_id ascending order labelled with screen_name, and a hall whose is_active is false renders its screen_name followed by the literal ' — out of service' and its option element carries no disabled attribute; and when scope_empty is true the scope line and the hall filter are both absent from the DOM rather than rendered empty, asserted against published strings rather than a test id SCR-RPT-01 does not publish - queryByRole('combobox', {name: 'Hall'}) returns null, no element in the DOM has an accessible name of 'All my halls' or of 'All halls', and no text node in the rendered DOM matches the regular expression ^Halls shown:
SourceRef: P-RPT-02 P-RPT-08 E7 S5 FR-ADR-011

Title: Render the dashboard's figures, its states and its period line
Description: Money is formatted from integer paise at render time only, a figure renders only when the whole response has arrived, and the three empty states render three different ways. The week period line owes two forms, because a week whose two dates fall in different years reads a wrong year against a money figure under the one-year form.
AcceptanceCriteria: takings_paise 2783331 from S-RPT-06's seed renders as the exact text ₹27,833.31 with Indian digit grouping, in --fr-font-mono with font-variant-numeric tabular-nums asserted from the figure element's computed style per the SCR-RPT-01 token table, formatted at the edge only - a walk over the full JSON of GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 (EP-RPT-01), GET /api/reports/showtimes?period=day&date=2026-08-14&limit=50&offset=0 (EP-RPT-02), GET /api/reports/scope (EP-RPT-03) and GET /api/reports/audit?from=2026-08-12&to=2026-08-12 (EP-RPT-04) finds no string value containing the character ₹ and none matching the regular expression \d+\.\d{2}; with the dashboard request held pending all four figure elements render the loading block and none carries a value, and on resolution all four carry values in the same render, asserted by snapshotting the four elements at both points, and after a period change the takings element reads the loading block and not ₹27,833.31 while the next request is pending; the period line renders 'Friday 14 August 2026' for day, 'Monday 10 August to Sunday 16 August 2026' for a week inside one year, 'Monday 29 December 2025 to Sunday 4 January 2026' for ISO week 1 of 2026 whose dates fall in two years, and 'August 2026' for month, all derived from a local anchor date by calendar arithmetic with no instant converted on the client; scope_empty true renders all four figures as the exact text '—', the occupancy bar and both tables absent from the DOM, and the single line 'No halls are assigned to this account. Ask an administrator to assign one.' on an element carrying no role='alert' and whose computed colour is not --fr-danger-ink; capacity 0 renders takings ₹0.00, occupancy '—' with the bar absent, and 'No shows were scheduled in this period.'; capacity above 0 with seats_sold 0 renders ₹0.00, '0.0 %' with the bar element's inline width 0%, and 'No seats were sold in this period.'; films_truncated true renders 'Showing the top 100 films by takings. The figures above cover every film in this period.' on an element carrying no role='alert' and whose computed colour is not --fr-danger-ink, and the four figures read the same values as in the untruncated case; the per-film caption reads 'Per film, in your halls' for a manager and 'Per film' for an administrator; the live-figures note renders two sentences for a manager and the first alone for an administrator, and queryByRole('link', {name: /change log/i}) returns null in a manager's DOM; and a per-show row with has_started false renders the exact text 'Still selling'

Title: Make the dashboard operable and announced, with only the per-film table sortable
Description: The per-show table cannot honestly be sortable, because EP-RPT-02 accepts no sort parameter and a client-side sort would reorder one page while claiming to describe the period. Every control in the focus order has a published string.
AcceptanceCriteria: On the day view of /dashboard on S-RPT-06's seed, with the per-show table on the first page of 214 rows, repeated userEvent.tab() calls from the top of the document are recorded until focus leaves the panel and document.activeElement at each stop is mapped to its containing region by Node.contains; the recorded regions are exactly, in this order and each contiguous, the period tablist, the period stepper, the hall filter, the change log link, the per-film table, the per-show table's scroll container and the per-show pagination - seven regions for an administrator and six for a manager, whose DOM contains no change log link - with no stop mapping outside those regions; five of the seven carry an accessible name SCR-RPT-01 publishes and are asserted by name - the tablist contributes one stop, the tab carrying aria-selected true, accessible name 'Day' on arrival; the stepper contributes two, named 'Previous day' then 'Next day' on the day view; the hall filter contributes one, the combobox whose accessible name is 'Hall'; the change log link contributes one, the link named 'Change log'; and the pagination contributes one on the first page, the button named 'Later shows', 'Earlier shows' being absent at the start of its range; the per-film table contributes six, its column header buttons in the published header order Film, Shows, Seats sold, Capacity, Occupancy, Takings, the first named 'Film, sort by this column' and the takings one 'Takings, sorted highest first. Activate to sort lowest first'; and the per-show table contributes one, the scroll container that contains getByRole('table', {name: 'Every show in this period'}) and carries tabindex='0', asserted by containment and position because SCR-RPT-01 publishes no accessible name for it and this criterion invents none; at every stop getComputedStyle(document.activeElement).outlineColor resolves to the computed value of --fr-focus-ring in the active theme; the period stepper's accessible names read 'Previous day' and 'Next day' on the day view, 'Previous week' and 'Next week' on the week view, and 'Previous month' and 'Next month' on the month view; the takings figure's accessible name is 'Takings, twenty-seven thousand eight hundred and thirty-three rupees and thirty-one paise' and the occupancy figure's is 'Occupancy, twenty-nine point five per cent' on S-RPT-06's seed; getAllByRole('columnheader') on the per-film table returns six, each containing a button and carrying aria-sort, and on the per-show table returns seven, none containing a button and none carrying aria-sort; a sortable header's accessible name is its text plus ', sort by this column' when unsorted, ', sorted highest first. Activate to sort lowest first' when descending and ', sorted lowest first. Activate to sort highest first' when ascending, and the takings header carries the descending form on first render; toggling a column and toggling back returns [(f['movie_id']) for f in rendered rows] to the list it held before the first toggle, every client-side re-sort falling back to title ascending then movie_id ascending; the occupancy bar carries aria-hidden='true' and the percentage text node is present in every state in which the bar element is; the element carrying aria-live='polite' contains 'Day, Friday 14 August 2026.' followed by the two figure sentences once per period change and contains 'Shows 51 to 100 of 214' after a page change, rendering 'Showing the only show in this period' when total is 1; a pagination control at the end of its range returns null from queryByRole rather than carrying a disabled attribute; when scope_empty is true queryByRole finds no hall filter, no table and no pagination control, and no element in the DOM carries a disabled attribute; each table's scroll container has computed overflow-x auto and at a 320 px viewport document.body.scrollWidth equals document.body.clientWidth; and an axe-core scan run through @axe-core/playwright with the tag set wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a and wcag21aa returns results.violations of length 0 in each of three states, each named here with the fixture that induces it - the success state, on S-RPT-06's seed; the scope_empty state, signed in as manager P holding zero manager_screen_assignment rows; and the films_truncated state, on S-RPT-08's 101-film seed of 101 distinct movie rows each carrying one showtime on screen 3 or screen 5 with starts_at inside [2026-08-13T18:30:00Z, 2026-08-14T18:30:00Z) and at least one confirmed captured booking, one film more than P-RPT-05's 100-row cap, which returns films_truncated true and films of length 100
SourceRef: P-RPT-05 P-RPT-06 E7 S5 FR-ADR-051

Title: Build the change-log screen, with both selects populated from the response
Description: The action select and the administrator select are populated from available_actions and available_actors and from nothing else - no hardcoded list, no second endpoint, and no staff directory exists in this product. Filters submit only on Apply, because a date pair is two fields.
AcceptanceCriteria: On /dashboard/audit the Action select's option values equal available_actions in order and the Administrator select's equal available_actors in order, rg -n 'showtime\.base_price_changed|movie\.published' frontend/src returns 0 hits so no action vocabulary is hardcoded, and the mocked fetch's recorded calls for the screen's whole lifecycle are GET /api/reports/audit requests and nothing else; the first options render 'Any action' and 'Any administrator' and selecting either produces a request URL carrying no action and no actor_user_id parameter; an empty option set renders the any option alone plus the help lines 'Nothing was changed in this period.' and 'Nobody changed anything in this period.' with neither select carrying a disabled attribute; the filters do not auto-submit, so typing a from date later than the current to fires no request at all, asserted by the recorded call count being unchanged; a date change that removes a selected option clears that filter and puts 'The action filter was cleared. That account made no changes in this period.' into the same element carrying aria-live='polite' that renders the result count, and selecting an action leaves the Administrator select's option values byte-identical and vice versa; the result count region reads '1 change.' at exactly one and '0 changes.' and '12 changes.' otherwise; a before/after pair renders the field name base_price_paise with 25000 and 30000 side by side, and the strings ₹250.00 and ₹300.00 appear nowhere in the rendered DOM; occurred_at renders '12 Aug 2026, 3:40 pm', and the strings '15:40' and '+05:30' appear nowhere in the row list, the panel's zone note carrying the zone once; the row list is a table whose six columnheader accessible names are exactly 'When', 'Who', 'Action', 'Record', 'Before' and 'After' in that order and which pages with a control named 'Load older changes', ending on 'That is the oldest change in this period.'; a manager reaching the route sees the exact text 'This page is for administrators.' with queryByRole returning no combobox and no table; and rg -n 'download|Blob|createObjectURL|text/csv|xlsx' frontend/src/features/reports/audit returns 0 hits and no element in the rendered DOM has an accessible name matching the regular expression (?i)export|download|copy all
SourceRef: P-RPT-11 P-RPT-10 E7 S5 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-051

Title: Prove the exclusions by absence
Description: The eighteen P-SCP rows describe capabilities this product deliberately does not have. This epic turns each into a test that fails if somebody builds the excluded thing by accident, and — where SRC-001 6.6 preserves an affordance for later — proves the affordance is still there and still exposed by nothing.

Title: Freeze the mounted route set against the published contract
Description: The 58-endpoint inventory in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json is the scope boundary in machine-readable form. A route mounted that is not in it is scope creep with a URL. This guard runs from the first phase that mounts a router and every later phase inherits it. It is one-directional on purpose: a mounted route absent from the contract fails, a contract route not yet mounted does not, because completeness belongs to the other lanes.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test collects every route mounted on the FastAPI application and asserts (a) the set difference mounted-minus-contract is empty against the 58 (method, path) pairs in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json, whose endpoint_count field reads 58; and (b) no mounted path matches the case-insensitive regex cancel|refund|validat|check-?in|export|download|\.csv|import|sync|tmdb|scan|pos/. Against the running application GET /api/export/bookings.csv, POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-2345/cancel, POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-2345/validate, POST /api/admin/movies/import and GET /api/pos/sales each return 404 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body matching the error envelope in contract.json conventions: error.code is the literal string NOT_FOUND and error.request_id is a non-empty string, because that envelope carries request_id on every error and not on 5xx alone.
SourceRef: P-SCP-05 P-SCP-06 P-SCP-10 P-SCP-11 P-SCP-14 S2 S3.8 SRC-001 §6

Title: Hold the process and dependency inventory to three processes and no excluded machinery
Description: Three long-running processes exist, not four, and nothing runs on a schedule. A scheduler, a QR encoder, a spreadsheet writer or a model SDK entering the dependency list is how an excluded capability arrives before anyone writes a screen for it, so the manifest is guarded, not only the code. The outbound-host allow-list is the last of the four assertions on purpose: three separate exclusions lean on this story, so each of the first three stands on its own artefact — a parsed compose file, a parsed manifest, a literal host string — and none of them needs the allow-list to hold.
AcceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml parses to exactly three entries under its top-level services key — api, worker and the static frontend/src — and no service whose name, image or command matches sched|cron|beat|celery; rg -niE 'apscheduler|celery|dramatiq|BackgroundScheduler|schedule\.every|crontab' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src/ scripts/ returns 0 hits once lines whose first non-whitespace characters are # or // are stripped, so a comment saying no scheduler exists does not fail the check; parsing backend/requirements.txt and frontend/package.json yields no dependency name matching qrcode|segno|barcode|zxing|reportlab|openpyxl|xlsxwriter|weasyprint|openai|anthropic|langchain|tmdb; rg -niE 'api\.openai\.com|api\.anthropic\.com|generativelanguage\.googleapis|bedrock-runtime|api\.themoviedb\.org' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src/ scripts/ returns 0 hits — this and the manifest check are self-standing and do not depend on the allow-list below; and a test that patches the HTTP client's send method appends every outbound request to a list, from which the sublist of requests whose host is not one of the configured SES, S3 and SQS endpoints has length exactly 0 for a run that completes one checkout end to end - it is that sublist and not the full list that must be empty, because the same run legitimately sends one message to the configured queue endpoint.
SourceRef: P-SCP-06 P-SCP-07 P-SCP-09 P-SCP-14 P-SCP-17 S2 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-006

Title: Enumerate configuration so no excluded capability can be switched on by a variable
Description: Configuration is the other door an excluded capability walks through. The settings model names every variable it reads, so a TMDB key or a sweep interval cannot be added without changing that enumeration. PAYMENT_PROVIDER carries the sharpest rule in the specification: it has no default, because a default is how a deployment becomes a fake shop silently.
AcceptanceCriteria: Iterating the Settings model's declared fields (Settings.model_fields) yields no field name matching TMDB|MOVIE_API|API_KEY|SCHEDULE|CRON|SWEEP; starting the API with PAYMENT_PROVIDER unset exits with a non-zero status, writes the literal string PAYMENT_PROVIDER to stderr, and a TCP connect to the configured port is refused; starting it with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe exits with a non-zero status and stderr contains the literal string simulated; and with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=simulated, GET /health/ready returns 200 with body field payment_provider equal to the string simulated, which contract.json's GET /health/ready 200 body requires it to carry.
SourceRef: P-SCP-06 P-SCP-07 P-SCP-12 S2 S7.9 FR-ADR-041

Title: Assert the excluded tables and columns are absent from the migrated schema
Description: A column is cheaper to add than to remove once rows exist, so the schema is where an excluded capability becomes permanent. This asserts the absences the specification names. Note one near-miss the test must not trip over: used_at exists legitimately on password_reset_token and is forbidden only on booking.
AcceptanceCriteria: After alembic upgrade head against an empty database, SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='booking' returns no name matching used_at|discount|fee|tax|refund|\bpoints\b|concession; SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' returns no name matching refund|loyalty|point|tier|membership|discount|coupon|voucher|convenience_fee|tax|concession|order_line|checkin|check_in; and the same query against table_name='users' returns no column name matching tier|\bpoints\b|loyalty|membership. The password_reset_token.used_at column is explicitly excluded from the check and must still exist.
SourceRef: P-SCP-02 P-SCP-03 P-SCP-10 P-SCP-16 S2 FR-ADR-040 FR-ADR-048

Title: Assert the preserved affordances exist and are not mistaken for excluded surfaces
Description: Excluded is not blocked. Three things exist in the schema precisely because v1 does not use them, and a later session reading the exclusions could delete all three as dead weight. This story fails if any of them is missing — asserting their absence would be the defect, not the guard. Their non-exposure is a separate story, S-SCP-14, because it cannot be tested until a booking exists. Whether the cinema filter control renders is E-BRW's rule and not this story's: this story asserts only that the payload carries the array.
AcceptanceCriteria: After alembic upgrade head, information_schema.columns shows table booking carrying a status column and a cancelled_at timestamp column that is_nullable = 'YES' with column_default NULL; SELECT count(*) FROM cinema returns exactly 1 after the seed runs; information_schema.table_constraints and key_column_usage show table screen carrying a NOT NULL cinema_id column under a FOREIGN KEY constraint referencing cinema(id); and GET /api/reference returns a body whose cinemas key is an array of length exactly 1. All four assertions are positive: each fails if the thing is absent.
SourceRef: P-SCP-11 S2 S2.5 SRC-001 §6.6 FR-ADR-010 FR-ADR-013

Title: Hold the role set at exactly four and prove no cinema-staff role exists
Description: SRC-001 4.3's staff member scanning a ticket is withdrawn and 5.5.3 with it. Four roles exist: guest, customer, manager, admin. The role set itself is PROVISIONAL under SRC-003 C-1 and this story asserts the count that is written down, not a count it chose; what is not provisional is the removal of the staff role, which the ruling kills explicitly.
AcceptanceCriteria: sorted(member.value for member in the application's Role enum) equals exactly ['admin', 'customer', 'guest', 'manager'] and len(Role) == 4; no member name matches staff|usher|door|gate|scanner|attendant; rg -niE 'cinema_?staff|door_?scanner|ticket_?validat' backend/app/ frontend/src/ returns 0 hits; iterating the model_fields of every Pydantic request model in backend/app/ finds no model declaring a field named role; and POST /api/auth/register with a body carrying role: staff returns 400 with error.code equal to the literal string REQUEST_INVALID.
SourceRef: P-SCP-10 P-SCP-15 S2 S3.1 FR-ADR-009 SRC-003 C-1

Title: Prove the admin has no way to withdraw a showtime, without ruling what withdrawal would do
Description: P-SCP-18 is not an exclusion — it is OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01, reserved as money and irreversible, and this story answers none of it. It asserts only what v1 is specified to do: the capability is absent from every surface. An unbuilt capability is recoverable and an unrefunded customer is not, which is why absence is the right shape while the row is open. No withdrawal flow, refund behaviour, notification or policy may be introduced by this story, not even as a placeholder.
AcceptanceCriteria: A route-table walk finds no route mounted under /api/admin/showtimes whose methods include DELETE and no mounted path containing withdraw or cancel: DELETE /api/admin/showtimes/1 returns 405 with error.code equal to METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and POST /api/admin/showtimes/1/withdraw returns 404 with error.code equal to NOT_FOUND; the rendered accessibility tree of the admin showtime list route and the admin showtime edit route contains no element with a control role whose accessible name matches the case-insensitive regex withdraw|cancel|delete|pull; and PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id} with a body property status, withdrawn or cancelled_at returns 400 with error.code equal to REQUEST_INVALID and error.details naming the rejected property.
SourceRef: P-SCP-18 S2 FR-ADR-023

Title: Prove the seat map carries no accessible marking, no pair linkage and no gap rule
Description: Every seat is sold individually and any available seat may be chosen. The guard matters most for the lock: a paired seat would turn a per-seat lock into a per-group lock, which is a materially harder concurrency problem, so the absence of pairing is a property the concurrency proof depends on. Recorded, not challenged: a real cinema in India operates under accessibility obligations and this rests on there being no real customers.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every object in the seats array of GET /api/showtimes/{showtime_id}/seatmap has a key set containing no key matching accessible|wheelchair|pair|couple|companion|gap|group, asserted against the response schema for that endpoint in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json and against a live response; SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='seat' returns no name matching those same tokens; POST /api/showtimes/{showtime_id}/holds for seats A-01 and A-03 on a row where A-02 is available returns 201 — no rule refuses the single-seat gap; and immediately after that hold, SCAN MATCH lock:seat:{showtime_id}:* returns exactly two keys, lock:seat:{showtime_id}:{seat_id of A-01} and lock:seat:{showtime_id}:{seat_id of A-03}, and no third — the per-seat key format P-HLD-08 publishes, one key per seat and never one per group.
SourceRef: P-SCP-13 S2 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-03 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-04

Title: Prove one responsive web interface exists and no native or installable artefact does
Description: The substitute the client named themselves is a website that works well on a phone. The guard has two halves: no native or app-store artefact anywhere in the repository, and the hardest case the responsive interface has actually working — the largest hall's seat map on a 375-pixel screen. The 220-seat figure is ASSUMED under OPEN-SCALE-02 and this story cites it as the design target the PRD names, not as a ruled hall size.
AcceptanceCriteria: A walk of every tracked path in the repository matches none of ios/, android/, *.xcodeproj, AndroidManifest.xml, *.webmanifest or capacitor.config.*, and parsing frontend/package.json yields no dependency name matching react-native|capacitor|cordova|expo; rg -niE 'serviceWorker|beforeinstallprompt' frontend/src/ returns 0 hits; and at a 375-pixel viewport the 220-seat hall's seat map container has scrollWidth greater than clientWidth while document.body.scrollWidth equals document.body.clientWidth, and getComputedStyle of a rendered seat cell returns width 24px at that viewport and width 24px again at a 1280-pixel viewport — 24px being the unchanged value of --fr-seat-size in docs/05 B DesignSystem/tokens.css, so the cell is never shrunk to avoid the scroll.

Title: Prove the public surface offers no upcoming section, no language switch and no recommendation
Description: Three exclusions share one surface — the shell, the listing and its controls — so they share one guard. Two near-misses must be checked and cleared rather than assumed: the Language filter is the film's language and not the interface's, and the default listing order is an ordering with a stated tiebreak, not a recommendation. Which sort orders a customer may choose is OPEN-SORT-01 and this story asserts only that the order is deterministic and identical between callers, not what the order should be.
AcceptanceCriteria: The frontend/src router registers no route whose path matches ^/(upcoming|coming-soon)$ and both URLs render the 404 view; the rendered accessibility tree of the application shell contains no element with a control role whose accessible name matches the case-insensitive regex language|locale|translate|coming soon|pre-sale|notify me|recommend|for you; rg -niE 'i18n|react-intl|formatjs|gettext|recommend' frontend/package.json frontend/src/ returns 0 hits; changing the listing's Language control issues a GET /api/movies carrying the query parameter language_id, and the document's html lang attribute and the accessible names of every link inside the navigation landmark are byte-identical before and after that change; and two consecutive calls to GET /api/movies with no sort parameter, one anonymous and one as a signed-in customer, return identical id sequences equal to the order published_at DESC then id DESC that contract.json's GET /api/movies 200 description states.
SourceRef: P-SCP-04 P-SCP-08 P-SCP-17 S2 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-044 SRC-003 OPEN-MODEL-01

Title: Prove no point-of-sale integration exists and name the writers against the seat constraint
Description: Seats sold online are the only seats this system knows about. The guard is that nothing imports or exports counter sales and that the set of code paths writing seat occupancy stays small enough to enumerate — which is also what would make a counter sale safe to add later, since it would be another writer against the same unique constraint. The writer check is an ORM event listener and not a text search on purpose: a SQLAlchemy insert contains no INSERT string, so a textual grep would report a clean result against code that writes freely. The operational consequence, that a seat sold at the counter renders available, is recorded in P-SCP-05 and needs no code.
AcceptanceCriteria: rg -niE '\bpos\b|\btill\b|counter_?sale|terminal_?sale' backend/app/ frontend/src/ returns 0 hits, and S-SCP-01's mounted-path regex already refuses any route path matching pos/; and a test registers a SQLAlchemy before_insert event listener on the booking_seat mapper, records inspect.getmodule(frame_info.frame).__name__ for every frame of the call stack at each insert across a run that exercises both the booking confirmation path and scripts/seed.py, and asserts the resulting set of originating modules has len() == 2, contains scripts.seed, and has as its only other member a module whose name starts with backend.app.domain. A third originating module fails the test.

Title: Prove no card data and no real provider exist anywhere, and that the demonstration line always renders
Description: A simulated payment that looks real to a customer is the worst failure this product can produce: it takes their seat, takes nothing else, and they find out at the door. So the guard is both halves — nothing card-shaped exists to be filled in, and every screen says so in words. No real provider is ever integrated, which makes the no-card-data rule trivially satisfiable; the point of the test is that it stays satisfied after someone adds a fixture out of habit. The card pattern is written narrowly for a stated reason: a bare card would match the footer line that discharges the requirement, so the pattern names card_?number and cardholder instead of card, and the criterion says what the one permitted exclusion would be if anyone ever widens it.
AcceptanceCriteria: No Pydantic request model in backend/app/ declares a field name matching card_?number|pan|cvv|cvc|expiry|expiration|cardholder, asserted by iterating every model's model_fields; rg -niE "$(printf 'card')_?number|cvv|cvc|expiry_?(month|year)|$(printf 'card')holder" backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src/ scripts/ - the pattern is ASSEMBLED FROM FRAGMENTS at run time so the test's own source does not carry it verbatim and cannot match itself, which is required here because backend/tests/ must stay IN scope (a card-shaped fixture is exactly what this guard exists to catch) returns 0 hits — the pattern deliberately does not include a bare card, because the footer literal below contains the words no card details, and if a later edit ever widens it to bare card then a line containing that one exact literal is the ONLY line that may be excluded and no other exclusion is permitted; rg -niE 'stripe|razorpay|payu|paypal|braintree|adyen' backend/app/ frontend/src/ scripts/ backend/requirements.txt frontend/package.json returns 0 hits, deliberately not run over backend/tests/ because S-SCP-03's negative start-up test must pass the literal stripe as the value it rejects; neither of these two checks depends on the allow-list test; the checkout screen renders no input whose name, id, autocomplete or associated label matches that same field pattern or the tokens cc-number|cc-exp|cc-csc; the exact string 'Demonstration environment. Payments are simulated and no card details are ever taken.' renders inside the single contentinfo landmark on /, the listing, the seat map, checkout and the confirmation page; and after a confirmed booking SELECT state FROM payment WHERE id = (SELECT payment_id FROM booking WHERE id = :id) returns captured - the column is state and the foreign key runs booking.payment_id to payment.id, so payment carries no booking_id column to select on, as S-PAY-05 asserts - that row's pending_at, authorized_at and captured_at are each non-null and satisfy pending_at <= authorized_at <= captured_at, and S-SCP-02's outbound recorder holds 0 requests to a host outside the configured SES, S3 and SQS endpoints for that run.

Title: Prove the charged total is the sum of the seat prices and carries no other line
Description: Four exclusions land on one figure — no food and beverage line, no loyalty balance, no discount or concession rate, no booking fee and no separate tax line. AcceptanceCriteria: For a booking of three seats priced 25000, 25000 and 30000 paise — 25000 + 25000 + 30000 = 80000 — POST /api/bookings stores booking.total_paise = 80000 and SELECT sum(price_paise) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = :id returns 80000, the total being the sum of the already-rounded per-seat prices and never a separately rounded figure; no response schema in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json and no live response body carries a key matching fee|booking_fee|convenience|tax|gst|vat|discount|promo|coupon|concession|loyalty|\bpoints\b|food|beverage|order_line; the top-level keys of GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{reference} whose names end in _paise are exactly ['total_paise']; POST /api/bookings with a promo_code or discount_code property returns 400 with error.code equal to REQUEST_INVALID; and the confirmation page's fact list renders exactly the five labels FILM, HALL, SHOWTIME, SEATS and PAID in that order and no sixth, PAID being the only monetary label on the page.

Title: Seat selection and the hold
Description: Everything between a customer looking at a seat map and a customer having seats that are provably theirs for 180 seconds: what a tap does, what the running total says, and the hold itself - acquiring it, its expiry, giving seats back and every way it can fail. A Redis lock provides the hold; the database's unique constraint on (showtime_id, seat_id) provides the truth.

Title: Render the four seat states from the three wire values
Description: The seat map carries exactly four rendered states - available, sold, held_by_other, held_by_me - over an enum the server emits with only three values, because the map is one shared cached payload and the server does not know whose session is reading it. The client decides held_by_me against held_by_other from its own hold token, and a chosen-but-not-yet-held seat reuses the held_by_me treatment.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given a payload from GET /api/showtimes/77/seatmap in which seat 402 carries state `held`: with no hold token in sessionStorage the cell renders fill --fr-seat-held-other with the `bar` mark and no border (COMPONENTS.md §1.4), its accessible name ends `held by another customer`, and it is not tappable; with a hold token in sessionStorage whose seat list contains 402 the identical payload renders 402 with fill --fr-seat-mine, a 2px --fr-seat-edge-mine border and the `check` mark, and its accessible name ends `held by you`; a seat id present in fr.selection but in no hold renders that same held_by_me treatment; rendering each of the three wire values against hold-token membership yields exactly four distinct (fill token, mark) pairs - (--fr-seat-available, outline), (--fr-seat-sold, hatch), (--fr-seat-held-other, bar), (--fr-seat-mine, check) - and exactly four distinct accessible-name endings - `available`, `sold`, `held by another customer`, `held by you` - asserted by two set comparisons each returning a set of size exactly 4, so no fifth rendering exists; a payload seat whose state is `held_by_me`, `held_by_other`, or any value outside the three wire values `available` / `sold` / `held` is rejected client-side and the screen renders `The seat map could not be loaded.` with a control reading `Try again`; a seat object arriving with no is_active field is rejected identically, and the test asserts the rejection rather than a default of true; a seat with is_active false renders with no fill, a 1px dashed --fr-rule border and a --fr-ink-muted number, keeps its place in the arrow-key grid, reads `Row C seat 12, Premium, out of service`, and does not activate on Enter or Space in any of the four states; the map is one tab stop and not 220, asserted by counting tabbable elements inside the map container as exactly 1.
SourceRef: P-SEA-02 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-051 SRC-001 §5.2.2

Title: Choose and unchoose seats without taking anything
Description: Selecting and deselecting is entirely client-side: no request is sent, no Redis key is written, no row is inserted, and nothing on the server distinguishes a guest looking at a seat map from a customer looking at one. Scarcity is consumed only at the hold. The live selection lives under the sessionStorage key fr.selection, which is a different key from fr.pending_selection (owned by E5 / P-ACC-13) and may not be collapsed into it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the map loaded, tapping seat C12 whose state is `available` adds it to the local selection, writes fr.selection in sessionStorage containing that seat id, and issues zero network requests (asserted by a request spy reporting 0 calls); tapping it again removes it and rewrites fr.selection; tapping a seat whose state is `sold`, a seat rendered held_by_other, or a seat whose is_active is false changes neither the selection nor fr.selection and issues zero requests; with ten seats chosen, an eleventh tap does not add the seat, the map does not change, and the note under the total reads `Up to 10 seats.` with the number interpolating MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING; reloading /showtimes/7 restores the selection from fr.selection and re-checks it against the freshly fetched map; fr.selection is deleted when the selection empties and when those seats become a hold; this story's code never writes fr.pending_selection, asserted by `sessionStorage.getItem('fr.pending_selection')` returning null after each of the tap cases above, after the eleventh-tap case and after the reload case; closing the tab with a selection and no hold issues zero requests, asserted by a spy on unload and beforeunload reporting 0 calls, and leaves zero Redis keys, asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:7:*` returning empty.
SourceRef: P-SEA-01 P-SEA-03 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-014 SRC-001 §4.1

Title: Show the running total in integer paise, summing only
Description: The price summary shows a total that changes with every selection and that is the figure the payment step will charge. The seat-map payload carries price_paise per seat already rounded by the server, and the client only sums integers - one implementation of the arithmetic, which is what removes the two-screens-disagree risk.
AcceptanceCriteria: With base_price_paise = 25000 and category uplifts Premium 1250 and Recliner 3333 basis points, so that the payload carries server-rounded price_paise of 28125 for Premium and 33333 for Recliner: selecting two Premium seats then three Recliner seats renders the total after each tap as `₹281.25`, `₹562.50`, `₹895.83`, `₹1,229.16`, `₹1,562.49`, and the final running sum is the integer 156249 paise; the rejected round-once-at-the-end path would give 156248 and the test asserts 156249; the client performs no multiplication, no division and no rounding, asserted three ways - the total after every tap is byte-equal to the integer sum of the payload's own price_paise values; the seatmap seat object carries price_paise and no uplift field at all, its properties being exactly id, row, num, gr, gc, cat, price_paise, state, is_active, asserted against the EP-BRW-06 response schema by a set comparison; and the 156249-not-156248 assertion above fails on any recompute-and-round path; with no seats chosen the panel keeps its full height, the total reads `₹0.00` and the note reads `Up to 10 seats.`; if any selected seat has no known price the total is not rendered at all (asserted by the total element being absent, not empty) and the primary action is disabled; a price_paise that is not a non-negative integer causes the payload to be rejected with `The seat map could not be loaded.` and a control reading `Try again`; the figure is rendered in --fr-font-mono with Indian digit grouping and the ₹ symbol, formatted from the integer sum at render time only, asserted by the integer 156249 rendering as `₹1,562.49` and the integer 0 as `₹0.00`; the price summary region contains one line per chosen seat plus one total row and nothing else, asserted by counting its line elements as exactly the number of chosen seats plus 1, and its rendered textContent matches the case-insensitive regex `tax|fee|discount|convenience|surcharge|gst` zero times, asserted by a regex sweep over that region.

Title: Announce a chosen seat that has gone, with no request sent
Description: A poll, a reload or a return to the tab re-checks the local selection against a fresh map and a chosen seat has gone. Nothing was requested so nothing answered: this notice carries no error code, and before this story the only announced surface on the screen branched on a code (journey defect J-XCT-08). The return-from-sign-in case is a different situation with a different string and belongs to P-ACC-13 in lane E5 - it is not rendered by this code path.
AcceptanceCriteria: After a poll, a reload or a return to the tab re-checks fr.selection against a freshly fetched map and finds chosen seat C12 is no longer `available`, the SCR-SEA-03 banner renders exactly `C12 is no longer available. It has been removed from your choices.`; the banner's rendered text is byte-equal to that sentence, so it carries no error code and no request id; it is announced exactly once, asserted by exactly one text insertion into the element carrying aria-live=assertive; it carries no in-banner action - no `--fr-accent-ink` underlined action element and no control whose accessible name is `Try again — reload the seat map` or `Choose seats again` - and it carries exactly one control, the dismiss control, whose visible label is `Dismiss` and whose accessible name is `Dismiss this message` (published by `SCR-SEA-03` Copy), asserted by counting controls inside the banner as exactly 1 and reading that one control's role as button and its accessible name; activating that control removes the banner from the DOM, asserted by a count of banner elements returning 1 before the activation and 0 after; the same test asserts that a `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` banner on this screen carries zero controls and is cleared instead by the next selection change, because `COMPONENTS.md` §6 and `SCR-SEA-03` both rule `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` NOT dismissible - this codeless notice is dismissible only because the seat has already left the selection and there is nothing to press; the seat leaves the selection, its line leaves the price summary and the total drops by exactly that seat's price_paise; zero network requests are issued for the selection itself, asserted by a request spy reporting 0 calls beyond the map fetch; the banner renders in the page's own scroll context pinned to the top of the viewport and reserves its own height, asserted by a seat cell holding keyboard focus having a bounding rectangle fully inside the viewport with the banner live; with two chosen seats gone in one re-check, one banner is shown and not two, asserted by a count of banner elements returning 1.
