Title: Acquire a multi-seat hold all-or-nothing, in ascending seat-id order
Description: One hold request names a set of seats and succeeds or fails as a whole; it never returns a partial success. Each seat's lock is one Redis key acquired with SET key token NX PX ttl in a single command - a process that dies between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a seat unbuyable forever. One token per hold, not one per seat; a second request on the same showtime extends the existing hold under its existing token and its unchanged expires_at.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds with seat_ids [418, 402, 410] from an authenticated customer issues exactly three Redis commands of the form `SET lock:seat:77:<id> <token> NX PX <ttl_ms>` in the order 402, 410, 418, each one single command - asserted against a Redis command log containing zero SETNX and zero EXPIRE on this path; on success it returns 201 with one hold_token of exactly 43 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet, one expires_at, every seat now under that token each with its own price_paise, and total_paise equal to their sum; when SET NX returns nil for 410 and a GET on that key returns a value that is not this customer's hold token, `lock:seat:77:402` is removed by the compare-and-delete Lua script, `lock:seat:77:418` was never written, the response is 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE with details.unavailable_seats ["C10"], and `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` and `lock:seat:77:418` both return 0 - zero seats are held afterwards; when SET NX returns nil and the key's value IS this customer's existing hold token, the request does not roll back, that key is not added to the rollback set, its PTTL is not raised, and the response is 201; a second request naming new seats returns 201 carrying the SAME hold_token and the SAME expires_at as the first, with each new key's PTTL at most the milliseconds remaining to that instant and never a fresh 180000; the response body carries every seat under the token and not only the seats this request added; after step 7 finds a committed booking_seat row for a seat whose lock was won, the request takes the rollback path and returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE; the hold's token is added to `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and each key to `instance:{instance_id}:holds`, both with the hold's TTL, asserted by SMEMBERS and TTL; `DEL cache:seatmap:77` is issued after the Redis lock writes and never before, asserted by command ordering in the log; no row is written to any PostgreSQL table by this endpoint, asserted by a SQL statement log containing zero INSERT and zero UPDATE.

Title: Validate every seat id server-side before any lock is touched
Description: The interface limit is a convenience; the hold endpoint is the enforcement point. Every seat_id must be an integer, must exist, must be a member of THIS SHOWTIME'S materialised seat set (P-ADM-14, lane E6 - not the screen's current seats, which are a different set), and must be active. Any failure rejects the whole request before any lock is touched.
AcceptanceCriteria: The fixture for showtime 77 labels seat id 4NN as row C seat NN, so 402 is `C2`, 407 is `C7`, 412 is `C12` and 419 is `C19`; the seat label inside every message below is the OFFENDING seat's own `row` concatenated with its `num` and never a fixed string, asserted by re-running the duplicate case with seat_ids [407, 407] and observing `Seat C7 was listed twice. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.` With the interface bypassed, POST /api/showtimes/77/holds returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and leaves the SORTED output of `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` equal to its sorted pre-call value - Redis fixes no ordering for KEYS, so the comparison is over the sorted key set and never over the raw reply - for each of: seat_ids [402, 402] with message `Seat C2 was listed twice. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.`; seat 419, which exists on screen 3 but is absent from showtime_seat for showtime 77, with message `Seat C19 is not part of this hall. No seats were held.`; seat 412, whose row in showtime_seat for showtime 77 has is_active false, with message `Seat C12 is out of service. No seats were held.`; and seat_ids [] with message `Choose at least one seat.`; the membership test is against the materialised set and not the screen, asserted by a test that inserts seat 419 into screen 3 AFTER showtime 77 was created and observes the hold refused with `Seat C19 is not part of this hall. No seats were held.` while seat 419 is holdable on a showtime created after it; membership and active are independent checks, asserted by seat 412, which IS in showtime_seat for showtime 77 and has is_active false, being refused by the active message and not the membership one; POST /api/showtimes/999999/holds returns 404 NOT_FOUND with `That showtime could not be found.`; the validation runs before the cap check and before any Redis command, asserted by the command log for each of the five cases being empty of any SET.
SourceRef: P-SEA-01 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-01 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-03 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-04

Title: Hold seats for 180 seconds from configuration, with the expiry fixed at acquisition
Description: The hold lasts 180 seconds read from SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS. SRC-002 §8.1.1's 7 minutes is superseded by erratum E-1 and is dead text; any document, test, fixture or comment stating 7 minutes is a defect. The expiry instant is computed once and never moves - not by polling, not by re-selecting a held seat, not by adding a seat, and there is no endpoint that moves it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180 and the injected clock at 2026-08-14T14:02:37.412Z, a granted hold returns expires_at 2026-08-14T14:05:37.412Z in UTC with milliseconds and every one of its keys reports PTTL in the range (179000, 180000]; `rg -n -F '7 minutes' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src scripts/` returns 0 hits - those three trees are the whole of the application, and `docs/` is deliberately outside the scope because this criterion's own text contains the phrase and would match itself; no hold duration is compiled in as a literal, asserted by re-running that same test with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=45 and no code change and observing expires_at at 2026-08-14T14:03:22.412Z with every key's PTTL in (44000, 45000]; re-sending the hold naming a seat this customer already holds returns 201 and leaves expires_at byte-identical and the key's PTTL not raised; adding a further seat with the injected clock at acquisition+60s returns the same expires_at and writes the new key with PTTL in (119000, 120000] rather than a fresh 180000; the generated OpenAPI document offers no way to move an expiry, asserted by the operations whose path begins /api/holds being exactly GET /api/holds/{hold_token}, DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token} and DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token}/seats/{seat_id}, and by a walk of every request body schema in the document finding zero properties named expires_at; boot exits non-zero when SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS is absent, non-integer or <= 0, and when PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS is greater than or equal to SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS * 1000 / 10 - at a 180-second hold, 17999 boots and 18000 exits non-zero; when the TTL elapses the keys are removed by Redis and by nothing of ours, asserted with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=2 by `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returning 1 immediately after acquisition and 0 once Redis's own expiry has passed - the test polls that EXISTS until it flips and never reads the application clock - by the Redis command log for that window containing zero DEL and zero UNLINK of that key, and by `rg -ni 'apscheduler|BackgroundScheduler|celerybeat|beat_schedule|crontab|schedule\.every' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src scripts/` returning 0 hits, so no scheduled process of ours exists that could have done it.
SourceRef: P-HLD-02 E2 S4 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-025 SRC-003 OPEN-HOLD-01 SRC-002 §E E-1 SRC-002 §7.1 SRC-001 §5.2.5

Title: Decide expiry by asking Redis, never by comparing clocks
Description: The server never compares the current time against expires_at to decide whether a hold is alive; it asks Redis whether the key exists and whether its value is this hold's token. expires_at exists for one purpose - to be rendered as a countdown on the client. A malformed token is 400 REQUEST_INVALID before Redis is touched and never 409 HOLD_EXPIRED, because a token of the wrong shape names no hold that ever existed and telling the customer their hold ended would be a false statement.
AcceptanceCriteria: With a hold acquired at 2026-08-14T14:02:37.412Z and SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180, so expires_at is 2026-08-14T14:05:37.412Z: while all of the hold's keys are present a confirm returns 201; when the hold's keys are gone the same request returns 409 with error.code HOLD_EXPIRED, asserted twice over the two ways the keys actually go - once with the test deleting them directly, and once with the hold acquired under SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=2 and the test polling `EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` until it returns 0 so that Redis's own TTL removed them; and - this is the assertion that proves the server compares no clocks - advancing the INJECTED APPLICATION CLOCK to exactly expires_at and then to expires_at plus 1s while the keys are still present returns 201 and never 409 HOLD_EXPIRED, because real Redis honours its own TTL and knows nothing about the injected clock, so a criterion asserting HOLD_EXPIRED at that instant would fail against a correct implementation; no test in this story reads the wall clock, asserted by `rg -n 'time\.sleep\(|datetime\.now\(|datetime\.utcnow\(|time\.time\(' backend/tests/` returning 0 hits; the liveness function takes no clock argument, asserted by inspect.signature listing no parameter named now, clock, at or instant and no parameter annotated datetime, and it performs no comparison against expires_at, asserted by the Redis command log for one liveness check containing exactly one GET of the hold's key and no other command; GET /api/holds/{hold_token} with a well-formed 43-character token matching no key returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with `The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged. Choose them again if they are still free.`; with a key present whose value is a different token it returns 403 HOLD_NOT_OWNED with the same sentence; with a token of 42 characters, of 44 characters, or of 43 characters containing `+`, `/` or `=`, it returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID with `This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.` and the Redis command log for that request is empty; a client whose clock is one minute slow still succeeds while the key lives, and one whose clock is fast is still accepted - both asserted by the server's answer being independent of any client-supplied instant, and by GET /api/holds/{hold_token} taking no query parameter and no request body at all, asserted against the EP-HLD-02 contract entry whose request query and body objects are both empty.
SourceRef: P-HLD-03 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-02 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-047 SRC-002 §8.1.4

Title: Cap a customer at ten seats held at once on one showtime
Description: A customer may hold at most MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING seats at any one moment on one showtime, counted from their live holds plus this request, checked before any lock is taken. The cap bounds CONCURRENT HOLDS and the size of one booking. It does NOT bound how many seats one customer may buy on that showtime over successive bookings - nothing does, that is OPEN-BULKBUY-01, open and reserved, and this story asserts the specified 201 rather than inventing a limit.
AcceptanceCriteria: MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING=10, interface bypassed. A first request naming 11 seats returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 10 seats for one showtime. You chose 11.` and `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged; a customer already holding 6 seats on showtime 77 requesting 5 more returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 10 seats for one showtime. You are holding 6 and chose 5 more.`, and the six existing keys keep their PTTL and the hold keeps its expires_at byte-identical; the same customer requesting 4 more instead returns 201 and the hold then carries 10 seats; a customer holding 10 on showtime 77 requesting 4 on showtime 88 returns 201 - the cap is per showtime; a customer who has BOUGHT 10 seats on showtime 77 and immediately requests 10 more on showtime 77 returns 201 with a hold carrying 10 seats, and `SCARD holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:77` reads 0 immediately after that purchase and 1 after the new hold, because the commit removed the spent token and nothing counts bought seats against the cap; the count is read from the set `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and the Redis command log for the cap check contains zero SCAN and zero KEYS commands; with MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING set to 6 and no code change all three of this story's strings re-render at the new cap - the note reads `Up to 6 seats.`, a first request naming 7 seats returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 6 seats for one showtime. You chose 7.`, and a customer already holding 4 requesting 3 more returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 6 seats for one showtime. You are holding 4 and chose 3 more.` - proving no literal 10 is shipped in any of the three, asserted by those three rendered strings and by `rg -in -F 'up to 10 seats' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src/` returning 0 hits.
SourceRef: P-HLD-04 E2 S4 FR-ADR-026 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-01

Title: Stop the guest at the hold, on the router, and not at the seat map or at payment
Description: A guest may browse, open a seat map, select seats and watch the total build. A guest cannot acquire a hold - the hold is the first authenticated action, which is the stricter option because an unauthenticated hold endpoint would let anyone lock a whole hall for three minutes with no account. Authorisation is applied once, on the router, as a dependency. Whether a MANAGER may buy a ticket is unruled (OPEN-MGRBOOK-01, open and reserved), so this story adds no prohibition and asserts the specified acceptance.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds with no Authorization header returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with `Sign in to hold seats. Your selection has been kept.`, and returns the same with an expired JWT; in both cases `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged; GET /api/showtimes/77/seatmap returns 200 for the same unauthenticated caller, so the guest is stopped at the hold and not at the map; the check lives on the router and not in the handler, asserted by replacing the hold handler body with a bare return and observing the 401 still produced; a hold request from a manager account and from an admin account each return 201, exactly as for a customer; with a guest selection present the primary action reads `Sign in to hold these seats` and pressing it writes the selection and opens the authentication step without issuing any request to the hold endpoint (request spy reports 0 calls); on return from authentication the primary action reads `Hold these seats`, the selection has been restored and re-checked against a freshly fetched map, and NO hold has been taken automatically - asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` returning empty until the action is pressed.
SourceRef: P-HLD-05 E2 S4 FR-ADR-014 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-009 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02 SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 SRC-001 §4.1 SRC-001 §7.4

Title: Check the sales cut-off at the hold and never at confirmation
Description: Sales close at starts_at + SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES, derived at evaluation time and never stored on the showtime row. PROVISIONAL: SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES = +15 means fifteen minutes AFTER the advertised start (SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03, FR-ADR-042). The alternative reading is fifteen minutes BEFORE and the two are half an hour apart; one message from the client reverses it, and reversing it changes one configured value, its sign, and three assertions in this story.
AcceptanceCriteria: SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15, showtime 77 starting 2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30, the cinema row carrying the IANA zone Asia/Kolkata. A hold request with the injected clock at 2026-08-14T19:44:59+05:30 returns 201; at 19:45:00+05:30 and at 19:45:01+05:30 it returns 409 SALES_CLOSED with `Sales for this showtime closed at 7:45 pm. Choose another showtime.` and `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged - the comparison is now >= sales_close_at; the cut-off is evaluated at the hold and nowhere else, asserted by a hold acquired at 19:44:59 confirming with 201 at 19:47:00, and by a second hold acquired at 19:44:59 under SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=3600 confirming with 201 with the injected clock at 20:30:00, 45 minutes past the cut-off - `redis EXISTS` on each hold's keys returns 1 immediately before its confirm, so each 201 is attributable to the cut-off not being re-checked and never to the hold having outlived it or not; sales_close_at appears in no column of the showtime table, asserted by schema.sql containing no `sales_close_at` inside the CREATE TABLE showtime statement; the comparison is evaluated in the cinema's zone read from the cinema row and never in the container's local time, asserted by a test running with TZ=UTC and still refusing at 19:45:00+05:30; GET /api/showtimes/77/seatmap after the cut-off returns 200 with showtime.sales_closed true and every seat unselectable, and the banner reads `Sales for this showtime have closed.`, or `Sales for this showtime have closed. You can still pay for the seats you are holding.` for a customer holding seats; setting SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=-15 with no code change moves the three assertions to 19:14:59 accepted and 19:15:00 and 19:15:01 refused; boot exits non-zero when SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES is absent and when it is non-integer, and exits 0 with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=-15, asserted by the process exit code in each of those three cases.
SourceRef: P-HLD-06 E2 S4 FR-ADR-042 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-045 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-001 §10.12

Title: Name the seats that went, immediately, and never blame the customer
Description: When one or more seats a customer wanted has gone, the response is 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and details.unavailable_seats carries the seat LABELS the customer reads, never internal ids. The interface names them, marks them unavailable on the map immediately, and leaves the rest of the selection exactly as it was. A first hold is all-or-nothing so nothing is held afterwards and the message says so; a request that EXTENDS a live hold is the one path on which seats genuinely are still held, and it is told so.
AcceptanceCriteria: A first hold for five seats losing C12 and C13 returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE with details.unavailable_seats ["C12","C13"] - customer-facing labels, asserted by each value equalling that seat's `row` concatenated with its `num` from the seatmap payload (`C` + `12` = `C12`), matching the anchored regex ^[A-Z]+[0-9]+$ with no prefix, suffix, whitespace or padding of any kind added anywhere else in this criterion, and never equalling `str(seat.id)` - the comparison is against the id rendered as a string, because a string value can never equal the integer id and an assertion that cannot fail proves nothing - and message `C12 and C13 were taken by another customer. No seats were held. Your other choices are still selected — change these two and press Hold these seats again.`; losing exactly one returns details.unavailable_seats ["C12"] and `C12 was taken by another customer. No seats were held. Choose a different seat and press Hold these seats again.`; the same two failures on a request that EXTENDS a live hold return `C12 and C13 were taken by another customer. Your hold is unchanged. Your other choices are still selected — change these two and try again.` and `C12 was taken by another customer. Your hold is unchanged. Choose a different seat and try again.`, and in both cases the existing hold's expires_at is byte-identical and every one of its keys' PTTL is within 1000 ms of its prior value and never increased (PTTL is a countdown on Redis's own clock and strictly decreases between two reads, so equality can never hold); a seat found already sold by the post-acquisition booking_seat check produces the same one-seat sentence; the client repaints each named seat with fill --fr-seat-held-other and the `bar` mark, its accessible name ending `held by another customer`, and never with --fr-seat-sold, the `hatch` mark or a name ending `sold` (P-HLD-07: a seat lost to another customer's hold is held_by_other, and becomes sold only when their booking commits); every other chosen seat remains in fr.selection after the failure, asserted by reading the key; details.unavailable_seats is a non-empty array on every SEAT_UNAVAILABLE response, asserted across all four cases; the interface branches on error.code, asserted by replacing message with arbitrary text and observing the same banner state; none of the four sentences above matches the case-insensitive regex `sorry|apolog|unfortunat|regret|!`, asserted by a regex sweep over them.
SourceRef: P-HLD-07 E2 S4 FR-ADR-026 FR-ADR-052 FR-ADR-029 SRC-001 §5.2.6

Title: Let a customer give seats back - one at a time, all at once, and after the hold has already gone
Description: Tapping a held seat gives that seat back; the secondary control gives the whole hold back. Both are the compare-and-delete Lua script against the hold's token, so a client can only release a lock it owns. The rest of the hold survives with the same expires_at. The whole-hold path is its own seven-step procedure and is NOT the per-seat one in a loop. A release racing a confirm is settled by ordering, with no in-flight flag and no error code of its own.
AcceptanceCriteria: DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token}/seats/402 on a live three-Recliner-seat hold at 33333 paise each returns 200 carrying two seats, total_paise 66666, and expires_at byte-identical to before; `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returns 0 and the other two keys' PTTL are within 1000 ms of its prior value and never increased (PTTL is a countdown on Redis's own clock and strictly decreases between two reads, so equality can never hold); the delete is the compare-and-delete script, asserted by issuing the same call with a different hold's token and observing the key still present and the response 403 HOLD_NOT_OWNED; releasing the LAST seat returns an empty seats array, deletes the hold record and removes the token from `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` (asserted by SCARD returning 0), after which the same customer immediately taking ten seats on that showtime returns 201; DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token} returns 204 with no body, compare-and-deletes every key in ascending seat_id order, removes them from `instance:{instance_id}:holds`, deletes the hold record, removes the token from the cap index, and issues `DEL cache:seatmap:77` AFTER the releases - asserted by the Redis command log ordering, with zero DEL of the cache key appearing before the first release; a compare-and-delete returning 0 for one seat because that key had already expired does not stop the loop, the remaining seats are still released and the response is still 204; DELETE of a seat that is not in the hold returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with `That seat is not part of your hold.`; DELETE of an already-expired hold returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED and issues NO `DEL cache:seatmap:77` at all, asserted by that key being absent from the command log for the request; a release landing before a confirm's Redis re-validation makes that confirm return 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with zero payment attempts recorded and nothing charged, and the release itself returns its normal 200 or 204; a release landing after the booking committed deletes nothing and the booking stands, asserted by `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=77 AND seat_id=402` returning 1, and that release returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED - the same answer this endpoint gives for any hold that no longer exists, because the commit removed the hold record - so no release is ever refused BECAUSE A CONFIRM IS IN FLIGHT, asserted by the (status, error.code) pairs observed across the two orderings being exactly (200, none) or (204, none) for the first and (409, HOLD_EXPIRED) for the second, with no third status and no code specific to a confirm being in flight.
SourceRef: P-HLD-08 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-03 E2 EP-HLD-04 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-026 FR-ADR-029 FR-ADR-045 SRC-002 §8.1.3 SRC-001 §5.2.2

Title: Count down from a server-issued instant, warn once at sixty seconds, and claim nothing at zero
Description: The hold response carries an absolute expires_at in UTC, not a duration and not a remaining-seconds count. The client renders m:ss by subtracting from its own clock and the server never trusts that arithmetic, so a wrong client clock produces a wrong display and never a wrong outcome. At zero the client stops, disables the payment action and states the hold has ended - it does not delete anything, release anything, or claim the seats are free, and it names no cause because a TTL, a shutdown drain and a re-acquired key are indistinguishable from inside the browser.
AcceptanceCriteria: The hold response carries expires_at as an ISO-8601 UTC instant with milliseconds and carries no duration field and no remaining-seconds field, asserted against the EP-HLD-01 response schema; the countdown component takes the current instant as a required parameter, asserted by rendering it with no `now` prop raising, and never reads a clock itself, asserted by rendering it with now = expires_at minus 75s under a fake timer holding the environment clock at expires_at plus one hour and still getting `1:15`; with now = expires_at minus 60s it shows `1:00` with the warning line `Less than a minute left. At 0:00 your seats are released and you will need to choose them again.` present, the bar and digits switching to --fr-countdown-urgent, and exactly one text insertion into the element carrying aria-live=polite; at now >= expires_at it renders `0:00` and never a negative value, disables the payment action and shows `Your hold has ended and your seats have been released. You have not been charged.`; with a confirm already in flight the same instant instead shows `Your hold has ended. We are waiting for the answer to your payment. Do not close this page.` and the in-flight request is not cancelled, asserted by the request spy showing no abort; the seat cells are NOT pre-emptively repainted at 0:00, asserted by each held cell keeping fill --fr-seat-mine and the `check` mark until the next poll payload arrives; the digits are not inside a live region, asserted by the element containing them having no ancestor carrying aria-live in the rendered DOM; the label reads `TIME LEFT`; the hold token and the Idempotency-Key are in sessionStorage and not localStorage, asserted by localStorage.length being 0; after a reload, GET /api/holds/{hold_token} returns the same expires_at and the countdown resumes at the correct remaining time; closing the tab issues zero requests, asserted by a spy on unload and beforeunload reporting 0 calls and by `redis EXISTS` on the hold's keys still returning 1.
SourceRef: P-HLD-09 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-02 E2 EP-HLD-02 FR-ADR-047 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-051 SRC-001 §5.2.5 SRC-001 §5.2.6

Title: Fail the hold, the hold read and the release loudly when Redis is unreachable
Description: If Redis is unreachable the hold endpoint returns 503 and never falls back to the database for locks, never proceeds without a lock and never degrades quietly. Confirmation also returns 503, because confirming without a live hold would rely on the database constraint alone - safe against overselling but wrong for the customer, who would discover at payment that they were confirming seats someone else was holding. A test that mocks a connection error proves the handler; only stopping the container proves the client's timeout configuration.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the Redis container actually stopped - not a mocked connection error: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with `Seat holds are unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.` and returns a response body rather than hanging; DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token} and DELETE /api/holds/{hold_token}/seats/{seat_id} return the same status, code and sentence; GET /api/holds/{hold_token} returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; the confirm endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with `We cannot complete your booking right now. You have not been charged. Try again in a few minutes. If you need help, quote {request_id}.` and the simulated provider records zero capture attempts; no code path substitutes PostgreSQL for a lock, asserted by the SQL statement log for each of those five requests during the outage being empty of any statement against seat, showtime or booking_seat, and containing zero `FOR UPDATE`; GET /health/ready returns 503 while GET /health/live returns 200 during the same outage; the Redis client is constructed with an explicit connect timeout equal to REDIS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 500) and an explicit per-command timeout equal to REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS (default 500), asserted by reading both off the client's configuration object in a test and finding each equal to the configured integer and neither None; boot exits non-zero when either variable is absent, non-integer or <= 0; the failure handler issues no Redis command, asserted by the command log for the failing request being empty; when Redis returns, the holds taken before the outage are gone, asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` returning empty BEFORE the next request is sent, and the next hold request then returns 201, after which that same command lists exactly the keys that request wrote and nothing else. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.
SourceRef: P-HLD-10 E2 S4 FR-ADR-028 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-052 SRC-002 §7.9 SRC-002 §7.4 SRC-002 §5.2.3

Title: Snapshot each seat's price at hold acquisition and never recompute it
Description: At acquisition the API computes the per-seat prices and stores them with the hold in Redis under the hold token; at confirmation those stored prices are used, not recomputed. The price a customer pays is the price that was current when their hold was granted, and the protection window is bounded by the hold itself so it needs no separate expiry. Extending a hold reprices nothing, so one hold may legitimately carry seats priced from two different base prices - that is this rule working, not a defect.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each seat's price is computed once as seat_price_paise = (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000) // 10000 in integer arithmetic, asserted by type(seat_price_paise) is int for every category and by a table of worked pairs that pins the rounding rule: base_price_paise 12345 with a 5000 bp uplift is exactly 18517.5 paise and the function returns 18518 and never 18517, so the rule is half-up and not truncation and not banker's rounding; base_price_paise 25000 with a 3333 bp uplift returns 33333 and with a 1250 bp uplift returns 28125; with base_price_paise 25000 and Recliner uplift 3333, two seats held at 19:32:37 store 33333 paise each under the hold token in Redis with the hold's TTL, asserted by reading the stored value and its TTL; an admin raising the showtime's base_price_paise to 30000 at 19:33:10 leaves those two stored prices at 33333 and the hold's total_paise at 66666, and the customer's total does not move; a third Recliner seat added to the same hold at 19:33:45 stores 39999, giving three seats, total_paise 106665 and expires_at still 19:35:37; confirming at 19:34:20 charges exactly 106665 paise and writes base_price_paise_applied 25000 for the first two booking_seat rows and 30000 for the third; the confirm path reads the stored prices and calls the pricing function zero times, asserted by a spy on that function; the next customer to take a hold after the change pays 39999 per Recliner seat; if Redis is unreachable at confirm so the stored prices cannot be read, the response is 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and nothing is charged; every money column on this path is declared bigint in schema.sql, those columns being exactly showtime.base_price_paise, booking_seat.price_paise, booking_seat.base_price_paise_applied and booking.total_paise, asserted by reading each of those four declared types out of schema.sql and finding bigint for all four; and a caller that skips the rounding function and passes a non-integer raises a type error rather than persisting, asserted by that call raising TypeError and by `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=77` returning the same number before and after it.
SourceRef: P-HLD-11 E2 S4 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-039 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-001 §5.2.4 SRC-001 §7.6

Title: Release this instance's holds on SIGTERM, and never depend on it
Description: Each API instance registers the keys of every hold it grants in a Redis set with the hold's TTL, and on SIGTERM it drains and runs the compare-and-delete release over that set. The registry lives in Redis and not in process memory because containers are stateless and a SIGKILLed process loses in-memory state before it can act on it. Expiry is the guarantee; this release is an optimisation on top of it, and correctness never depends on it running.
AcceptanceCriteria: A hold granted by instance i-1 adds each of its keys to `instance:i-1:holds` with the hold's TTL, asserted by SMEMBERS listing them and TTL matching the keys' PTTL to within one second; sending a real SIGTERM to that running container causes it, in order: to stop accepting new connections, to let in-flight requests finish, then to compare-and-delete every key in `instance:i-1:holds`, delete each affected hold record, remove each token from `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and issue `DEL cache:seatmap:{showtime_id}` once per showtime touched, then exit with code 0 - after which `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returns 0, SCARD on the cap index returns 0, and the same customer immediately re-requesting that seat receives 201; a key in the registry whose current value is another hold's token is left present, asserted by GET returning that other token unchanged; SIGKILLing the container instead leaves the keys present with their PTTL still counting down, asserted by `redis PTTL lock:seat:77:402` returning a positive value after the kill, and they are gone once Redis expires them with no process of ours having run, asserted with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=2 by `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returning 0 once Redis's own expiry has passed - the test polls that EXISTS and never reads the application clock - and by `rg -ni 'apscheduler|BackgroundScheduler|celerybeat|beat_schedule|crontab|schedule\.every' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src scripts/` returning 0 hits, so no scheduled process of ours exists that could have done it; a confirm in flight when SIGTERM arrives completes and its booking_seat rows are committed, asserted by `SELECT count(*)` returning 1 for that pair after the exit; the release step is best-effort - a test that makes the compare-and-delete fail for one key still sees the process exit 0 and the remaining keys released, asserted by that exit code and by `redis EXISTS` returning 0 for every key that was in `instance:i-1:holds` except the one whose delete was made to fail, which `redis GET` still shows holding this hold's token.

Title: Prove exactly one winner among fifty simultaneous hold requests
Description: The never-waivable concurrency gate. This is Stage A of the proof and it fires at the HOLD endpoint, where the Redis lock decides the winner. The constraint-drop red proof is Stage B, it belongs to P-XCT-01 in lane XCT, and it may not be run against this criterion: with the constraint dropped this same run still produces exactly one winner because every loser was refused by SET NX and the constraint was never reached, so reading that as a red proof proves nothing and reading it as a failure blocks a story for a defect that is not there.
AcceptanceCriteria: `scripts/stress_seats.py --showtime 77 --seat 402 --n 50 --base-url <url>` run with fifty distinct seeded authenticated customers reports exactly 1 response of HTTP 201 and exactly 49 responses of HTTP 409 whose error.code is SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and whose error.details.unavailable_seats is ["C2"]; the script records each request's start instant and exits non-zero with `not concurrent` when the spread between first and last exceeds STRESS_CONCURRENCY_SPREAD_MS, default 100 - a run whose spread is inside the threshold is required for a pass; after the winner confirms, `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id = 77 AND seat_id = 402` returns exactly 1; zero winners fails, and any loser returning 500 rather than 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE fails; the rate limiter runs normally throughout, asserted by RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_USER_PER_MIN reading 20 and RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN reading 60 in the running API container's environment during the run, by the run recording zero 429 responses, and by every request the script issues carrying only the Authorization and Content-Type headers, asserted by capturing the outbound headers; the same script run against the deployed environment by changing only --base-url produces the same three figures; this story asserts nothing about a dropped unique constraint, asserted by `rg -in 'drop constraint' scripts/stress_seats.py` returning 0 hits - the red proof is P-XCT-01 Stage B; the unique constraint on (showtime_id, seat_id) is total with no WHERE clause, asserted by `SELECT pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u'` returning exactly `UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id)`, and it is created by the same migration that creates the booking_seat table, so it exists before any booking row can, asserted by exactly one file under backend/migrations/versions/ containing both the creation of booking_seat and that unique constraint, and by no other file under that directory adding or dropping it.

Title: Publish this lane's message set, with a stable code and one substitution rule
Description: Every failure on this lane's endpoints returns one envelope; the interface branches on code and never on message text. Two rules govern the whole set: singular at exactly one offending seat and plural at two or more, counted over offending seats and not over the request; and a closing clause with two forms - `No seats were held.` on a first hold, `Your hold is unchanged.` on a request that extends a live hold, because on an extend the first sentence would be contradicted by the countdown, the held cells, the heading and the cap, all on the same screen.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every failure response on the four hold endpoints is `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...,"details":...,"request_id":...}}` with request_id present including on 500s; a table-driven test asserts the exact HTTP status, error.code and verbatim message for all 24 rows of the lane's message set, including `Seat C12 was listed twice. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.` at one offending seat and `Seats C12 and C13 were listed more than once. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.` at two; the singular renders at exactly one offending seat and the plural at two or more, counted over offending seats - asserted by a five-seat request carrying one duplicate rendering the singular; every offending seat is named, in submission order, joined `C12, C13 and C14` with no serial comma, never truncated and never summarised as a count; the closing clause substitution applies to exactly eight rows - the two SEAT_UNAVAILABLE-at-hold pairs and the six seat-level VALIDATION_FAILED strings - and to no other row, asserted by a test that runs each of the 24 rows once as a first hold and once as an extend and finds exactly eight sentences differing; each of the two SEAT_UNAVAILABLE extend strings ends with the characters `try again.` and contains neither `Hold these seats` nor `press`, asserted by string tests on those two published rows; request_id is rendered to the customer on 5xx only, asserted by a 422 body containing no `quote` and a 500 body containing `If you need help, quote `; a 429 carries Retry-After 3 with `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.` when the per-user bucket refused and Retry-After 1 with `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` when the per-IP bucket refused, the header value and the number in the sentence being the same value; none of the 24 published strings matches the case-insensitive regex `traceback|File "|SELECT |INSERT |UPDATE |psycopg|sqlalchemy|\.py\b|booking_seat|showtime_seat|redis://|postgres://|Error:`, asserted by a regex sweep; the set of error.code values the table-driven test asserts, deduplicated, is equal to the set of codes the four hold endpoints declare in the API contract, asserted by a set comparison, and every row asserts both a status and a code.

Title: Implement the seat lifecycle exactly as the normative state machine
Description: One seat, for one showtime, as seen by one customer session, is in exactly one of five states at every instant, and every one of twenty-nine inputs has a defined result in every state. The machine is normative: a behaviour not in the table is a defect, and an input handled differently from the table is a defect. No endpoint exposes the lifecycle state, so every assertion is made against its observable projection - the lock key's value, the booking_seat count, the wire state, the rendered accessible name and the test's own in-flight confirm. held_by_me_paying is a lifecycle state and not a fifth rendered map state - it renders identically to held_by_me, so its projection differs from held_by_me's only by the confirm the test itself issued.
AcceptanceCriteria: The machine is asserted through the observable projection of each state, so that no test-only inspection endpoint is added: the projection is the triple (`GET lock:seat:77:402`, `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=77 AND seat_id=402`, the seat's `state` in GET /api/showtimes/77/seatmap) together with the rendered cell's accessible name and whether the confirm request this test itself issued has returned - `available` is (nil, 0, `available`); `held_by_me` is (this session's hold token, 0, `held`) with the name ending `held by you`; `held_by_other` is (a token that is not this session's, 0, `held`) with the name ending `held by another customer`; `sold` is (any, 1, `sold`); and `held_by_me_paying` is `held_by_me`'s projection while a confirm this test issued has passed its Redis re-validation and has not yet returned, which the test knows because it made the request. On that projection: the fenced ```transition block of P-SEA-06 in `docs/03 PRD/FrontRow_PRD.md` parses as JSON, its `states` has length 5, its `inputs` has length 29, its `transitions` has length exactly 145, no entry is missing `to`, `guard` or `user_sees`, and the set of its (from, input) pairs equals the 145-element product of states and inputs, asserted by a set comparison; for every one of the 145 the implementation reaches the projection of that row's `to` state, and wherever the row's `guard` names an HTTP status and error code, that status and that code are what the request returns; the four reachability edges hold - `held_by_me` from `available` by HOLD_ACQUIRE_OK, `held_by_me_paying` from `held_by_me` by CONFIRM_START, `sold` from `held_by_me_paying` by CONFIRM_COMMIT, `held_by_other` from `available` by OTHER_ACQUIRES; SIGN_OUT from `held_by_me` leaves `GET lock:seat:77:402` returning nil and sessionStorage holding zero keys with the `fr.` prefix; TAB_CLOSED from `held_by_me` leaves the key present with its PTTL within 1000 ms of its prior value and never increased (PTTL is a countdown on Redis's own clock and strictly decreases between two reads, so equality can never hold) and issues zero requests, asserted by a spy on unload and beforeunload reporting 0 calls; SALES_CUTOFF_PASSES changes no seat's projection in any of the five states, asserted by comparing the triple before and after; CONFIRM_PAYMENT_FAILED_HOLD_LIVE leaves the key holding this session's token and CONFIRM_PAYMENT_FAILED_HOLD_GONE leaves it nil; INSTANCE_KILLED_PRECOMMIT leaves booking_seat count 0 with the key still holding this session's token, and INSTANCE_KILLED_POSTCOMMIT leaves booking_seat count 1; `held_by_me_paying` and `held_by_me` produce byte-identical rendered cells, asserted by a DOM comparison, so the map still carries exactly four rendered treatments over three wire values; each transition whose `guard` begins `impossible:` carries a test that attempts it and observes the alternative that guard names - for example a confirm against a seat whose projection is `available` takes CONFIRM_HOLD_GONE and returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with the simulated provider recording zero capture attempts; the block's `inputs` array is exactly the 29 named inputs and contains no `SHOWTIME_WITHDRAWN`, asserted by set equality, because no withdraw capability exists in v1 (OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01 is open and reserved).

Title: Let sold win over any lock when the seat map is assembled
Description: A seat's map state is computed from two sources - a booking_seat row in PostgreSQL and a lock key in Redis - and sold always wins. Locks are released after commit, not before, so there is always a window in which both exist; if the container dies inside it the lock survives against a seat that is already sold. Without an explicit precedence rule two correct sources produce two different answers for the same seat.
AcceptanceCriteria: With a committed booking_seat row for (77, 402) AND a live key `lock:seat:77:402`, GET /api/showtimes/77/seatmap reports seat 402 with state `sold` and never `held`; with only the lock present it reports `held`; with neither it reports `available`; with only the booking row it reports `sold`; the set of distinct state values across every seat in the payload is a subset of {available, sold, held}, asserted by a set comparison - neither held_by_me nor held_by_other can be emitted by the server; a residual lock on a sold seat produces no banner element in the rendered page and the cell renders fill --fr-seat-sold with the `hatch` mark and no border (COMPONENTS.md §1.4), its accessible name ending `sold`, asserted by rendering SEAT 402'S OWN CELL from the payload taken with the residual lock present and from the payload taken with it absent and finding the two byte-identical - the same seat in both renderings, because two DIFFERENT seats' cells carry different ids, numbers, grid positions and accessible names and can never be byte-identical against a correct implementation; with Redis unreachable the endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and the customer sees `The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.` - the map is not served without hold state, because the rate limiter reads Redis and fails closed before the cache is consulted; the precedence is implemented once, asserted by replacing the sold-wins comparison with a raise and observing all four of the cases above raise, none of them still answering.
SourceRef: P-SEA-05 E2 S4 FR-ADR-024 FR-ADR-029 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-058 SRC-002 §8.1.5

Title: Receipt and entry
Description: Everything between the money being taken and the customer standing at the entrance: the booking reference, the confirmation page, the transactional outbox, the SQS worker, the SES send, the resend control and the manual door check. The emailed receipt carrying a unique booking reference is the customer's only proof of purchase and their only way into the hall, and there is no QR code, no scanner and no validation endpoint.
SourceRef: E4 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAIL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02

Title: Generate a unique booking reference inside the confirm transaction
Description: Every confirmed booking is given one 8-character reference - 7 characters drawn from a 26-character alphabet by a cryptographically secure source, then 1 check character from the same alphabet (SRC-004 R-5) - stored uppercase under a UNIQUE constraint, generated inside the booking transaction with no endpoint that mints one. OPEN-REFCHAR-01 is RULED by SRC-004 R-5: the alphabet is SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01's set minus Z, S, B and G, and the 8th character is a check character over the first 7 whose algorithm is recorded in the code that implements it. ck_booking__reference_charset enforces the alphabet and the length in the database; it cannot verify the check character.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the draw stubbed to known values, a confirmed booking gives `SELECT length(reference), reference = upper(reference) FROM booking WHERE id=:b` returning `8, true`; over 1000 generated references `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference !~ '^[23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{8}$'` returns 0, so none contains 0, 1, B, G, I, L, O, S, U or Z and none carries the FR prefix or a hyphen; for each of those 1000 references the 8th character equals the check character the generator's own check function computes over the first 7; a second INSERT of an already-stored reference fails and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference=:dupe` stays at 1, so the UNIQUE constraint is the guard rather than the collision arithmetic; with the draw stubbed to return an already-stored value 4 times then a free one, the confirm returns 201 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference=:free` returns 1; with the draw stubbed to collide 5 times the confirm returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:u` returns 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=:s` returns 0; `rg -n 'import secrets' backend/app` returns at least 1 hit and `rg -n 'random\.' backend/app` returns 0 hits.
SourceRef: P-TKT-01 FR-ADR-015 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 SRC-004 R-5 E4 S4

Title: Normalise a typed reference and correct nothing
Description: A reference supplied as input is uppercased and stripped of whitespace, hyphens and an optional leading FR, then matched by equality. Nothing is mapped, aliased or guessed, because a system that guesses can admit the wrong person, and the three ways a lookup can fail are made indistinguishable so the endpoint is not an enumeration oracle.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a booking whose stored reference is `ABCDEFGH`, `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` as its owner returns 200 for each of `FR-ABCD-EFGH`, `fr abcd efgh`, `abcdefgh` and `  FR-abcd-EFGH  `; it returns 404 NOT_FOUND for `FR-0BCD-EFGH` (a zero typed for O), `FR-1BCD-EFGH` (a one typed for I) and `FR-ABCD-EFG` (7 characters), and the zero is not mapped to O; the Cyrillic-homoglyph input `АВСDEFGH` (U+0410 U+0412 U+0421 followed by ASCII DEFGH) returns 404, so the uppercasing folds no non-ASCII character onto an alphabet member; a 65-character path value returns 404 with a database query counter of 0 for the request; the match is an equality predicate, asserted over the captured statement log for the request, against which `rg -in -e 'like ' -e 'similarity\(' -e ' ~* '` returns 0 hits; the status and the parsed body of a malformed reference, an unknown well-formed reference and another customer's well-formed reference are compared pairwise with error.request_id deleted from each - the envelope carries one on every error and it is unique per request, so the raw bytes legitimately differ there and nowhere else - and every pair is equal, error.code, error.message and error.details included, so the endpoint is no enumeration oracle.
SourceRef: P-TKT-02 FR-ADR-015 EP-TKT-01 E4 S4

Title: Read one booking by its reference, on ownership alone
Description: EP-TKT-01 returns the facts a customer needs at a door for a booking whose user_id equals their own. The role is never consulted, so an admin reads their own bookings and nobody else's, and the receipt's dispatch state is deliberately not in the response because rendering a failed state is OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01, which is open and reserved.
AcceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-EFGH` as the owner returns 200 whose body keys are exactly `reference, film_title, hall_name, starts_at, seats, total_paise, paid_at, receipt_email_address`; with the stored showtime instant `2026-08-21T13:45:00Z` and the cinema row's offset at +05:30, `starts_at` is `2026-08-21T19:15:00+05:30` as one field, and no second local-time field exists; `seats` is `[F7, F8, F9]` for seat rows inserted in the order F9, F7, F8; `total_paise` is `84372` read from the stored column, asserted by mutating the seeded base price after the booking and re-reading the same value; the identical request made by a signed-in admin who does not own the booking returns 404 whose parsed body, with error.request_id deleted, equals the unknown-reference 404's parsed body with that same field deleted - the envelope carries one on every error and it is unique per request; the body contains none of the keys `status`, `cancelled_at`, `receipt_status`, `dispatch_seq`; the ownership rule lives in one router dependency and not in the handler, asserted by replacing that single dependency with a pass-through in the test application and observing the same non-owner request then return 200.
SourceRef: P-TKT-09 P-TKT-02 EP-TKT-01 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-018 E4 S6

Title: Show the reference on the confirmation page, independently of the email
Description: SCR-TKT-01 renders the reference and the booking facts the moment a booking is confirmed and on every later visit; it never states that an email has been sent, because at that moment it has not been. The receipt sentence is shown only when the confirm response is present in the client's navigation state, so a reload renders the later-visit state, and no replacement sentence is written for it because OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01 reserves what a customer is told about a receipt that may already have failed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Rendering `/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH` with the confirm response present in navigation state shows the h1 `Your booking is confirmed.`, the label `BOOKING REFERENCE`, the reference `FR-ABCD-EFGH`, the fact labels `FILM HALL SHOWTIME SEATS PAID`, the entry line `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`, the policy line `This booking cannot be changed, cancelled or refunded.` and exactly one occurrence of `A receipt is on its way to name@example.com.`; rendering the same route with no navigation state shows the same h1, reference block, facts, entry line and policy line and zero occurrences of each of `on its way`, `has been sent`, `was sent` and `delayed` in the rendered DOM's textContent; the loading state renders the reference element with a textContent whose length is 0, so no placeholder string of any length is present; the reference element's accessible name is `F R, A B C D, E F G H`; focus is on the h1 after arrival and the tab order is heading, reference, copy control, facts, resend control; the copy control writes `FR-ABCD-EFGH` to the clipboard and announces `Reference copied.` in a live region.
SourceRef: P-TKT-03 FR-ADR-048 SCR-TKT-01 E4 S5

Title: Commit the receipt_dispatch and outbox rows with the booking
Description: The receipt job exists only if the booking does: one receipt_dispatch row and one outbox_message row are inserted inside the booking transaction, immediately before commit, so there is no post-commit send with no record. No customer data travels in the payload, and the topic vocabulary has exactly two members because the account lane's password-reset email uses the same table, relay and worker.
AcceptanceCriteria: After one confirmed booking, `SELECT status, dispatch_seq, attempts, claimed_at, sent_at, ses_message_id, last_error FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` returns exactly one row reading `pending, 1, 0, null, null, null, null`, and `SELECT topic, status, attempts FROM outbox_message WHERE payload->>'booking_id'=:b` returns exactly one row reading `receipt.send, pending, 0`; the sorted payload key set equals `booking_id, dispatch_seq, message_version, request_id` and the payload text contains no @ character, no seat label and no amount; an attempted insert with `topic='receipt.render'` does not commit and `SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message WHERE topic='receipt.render'` returns 0 afterwards, and the same two assertions hold for a `receipt.send` payload carrying a fifth key and for one with `message_version` missing - this criterion asserts the observable outcome and names no mechanism, so GOAL_08 may implement the guard as a CHECK constraint, a trigger or application validation; a `password_reset.send` payload whose key set is exactly `message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id` commits and `SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message WHERE topic='password_reset.send'` returns 1; forcing the outbox insert to fail leaves `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference=:r` at 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=:s` at 0; a second `receipt_dispatch` insert for the same booking_id does not commit and `SELECT count(*) FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` stays at 1.
SourceRef: P-TKT-04 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-059 E4 S4

Title: Bound the fast-path queue send and relay what it leaves behind
Description: The queue send runs inside the confirm request after the commit and the response is emitted after it returns, so it is bounded by QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (2000, ASSUMED, no source states a figure) with SDK-level retry disabled so the bound is the value and not a multiple of it. Anything it leaves pending is relayed on the worker's existing receive loop; there is no scheduler and none may be added.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=2000` and the queue client stubbed to block against an injected clock, the confirm returns 201 no later than commit plus 2000 ms, the stub records exactly 1 SendMessage attempt, `SELECT status FROM outbox_message WHERE id=:o` reads `pending`, one ERROR line carrying the request_id is emitted and the response body carries no mention of the queue; with the queue reachable the same confirm leaves that row `sent` with sent_at non-null while `SELECT status FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` still reads `pending`; with `OUTBOX_RELAY_MIN_AGE_SECONDS=30` a worker poll at commit plus 29 injected seconds selects zero rows and a poll at commit plus 31 injected seconds selects the row with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in a bounded batch, sends it and marks it `sent` - outbox_message.created_at is written from the injected clock and the age threshold is bound into that statement from the same clock, asserted by `rg -n 'now\(\)|CURRENT_TIMESTAMP|statement_timestamp' backend/app/workers` returning 0 hits, because the database's clock does not move when the injected one does and a relay written against it would select the row at 29 s and at 31 s alike; the boot-time configuration check exits non-zero with no port bound when `QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS` exceeds one tenth of SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (20 s), asserted by starting the process with 2000 and 20 and again with 2100 and 20; `rg -in -e apscheduler -e celery -e BackgroundScheduler -e croniter -e crontab -e 'schedule.every' -e 'add_job\(' backend/` returns 0 hits, and `backend/` contains no file named `beat.py`, `scheduler.py` or `crontab`.
SourceRef: P-TKT-04 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-059 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01

Title: Claim the send before calling SES so one booking has one sender
Description: The worker branches on topic first, then claims the receipt send with a conditional UPDATE on the row the booking transaction already created; it transitions that row and never inserts one. Zero rows means another delivery owns the send, it is already sent, or the message carries a stale dispatch_seq. The claim makes two senders impossible; it does not make two sends impossible, which S-TKT-08 states.
AcceptanceCriteria: Delivering the same receipt.send message twice produces exactly 1 SES SendEmail call, asserted by the mail-port stub's call count, and `SELECT status, attempts FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` reads `sent, 1`; with `RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS=900`, receipt_dispatch.claimed_at written from the injected clock and the staleness threshold bound into the conditional UPDATE from that same clock - asserted by `rg -n 'now\(\)|CURRENT_TIMESTAMP' backend/app/workers` returning 0 hits, because a claimed_at taken from the database's clock is not moved by advancing the injected one and every age below would then be measured against the wrong origin - a delivery against a `sending` row whose claimed_at is 120 injected seconds old makes 0 SES calls, deletes the message, leaves attempts unchanged and logs one INFO line, while the same delivery at 960 injected seconds reclaims the row, increments attempts by 1 and makes 1 SES call; deliveries against `sent`, against `suppressed`, and against a row at dispatch_seq 2 when the message carries 1 each make 0 SES calls and delete the message, and the suppressed case logs one WARNING naming the booking_id; a message whose topic is `receipt.print` makes 0 SES calls and is NOT deleted, asserted by the queue stub still holding it; a receipt.send message whose booking_id resolves to no confirmed booking is deleted and logged, and the same deletion rule is not applied to password_reset.send; `rg -in 'insert into receipt_dispatch' backend/app/workers` returns 0 hits; and the regression guard on the deployment's two orderings, which no test can read off a Zone C queue, is that the table row of `docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md` whose first cell is `9` contains each of the literal strings `visibility timeout must be LESS THAN`, `RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS`, `maxReceiveCount`, `must be GREATER THAN`, `ceil(stale / visibility)` and `8 at the worked pair`.
SourceRef: P-TKT-05 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-056 FR-ADR-059 E4 S4

Title: Bound the SES call, and treat a timed-out send as failed and retryable
Description: SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (5000, ASSUMED, replaced by the phase 7 load test) stops a hung call holding the claim in sending for the full 900-second stale threshold. A timed-out send is recorded failed and is retried, so a send that in fact succeeded can deliver a second identical receipt: that is a stated limit on FR-ADR-032's guarantee, chosen deliberately because the alternative leaves a paying customer with nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=5000` and the mail-port stub blocking against an injected clock, the worker abandons the call at exactly T plus 5000 ms and `SELECT status, sent_at, ses_message_id, last_error FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` reads `failed, null, null` with last_error containing `timeout` and not containing the SES refusal string; the queue message is not deleted, asserted by the stub still holding it; redelivering that message claims the failed row and produces a SECOND SES call, and the test asserts that second call is made rather than asserting it is prevented, so no criterion in this lane claims a duplicate receipt is impossible; an SES error response produces the same failed row with last_error carrying the SES error string, distinguishable from the timeout case by that string; the timeout bound is read from configuration and not typed, asserted by `rg -n '5000' backend/app/workers` returning 0 hits and by re-running the same test with `SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=1200` moving the abandon point to exactly T plus 1200 ms; the process refuses to start when MAIL_PROVIDER or SES_SENDER_ADDRESS is unset, asserted by a non-zero exit and no port bound.
SourceRef: P-TKT-05 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-060 FR-ADR-053 E4 S4

Title: Render the receipt with everything needed at a door and nothing else
Description: SCR-TKT-02 carries the reference, seats, hall, showtime, film and amount in a plain-text part and a matching minimal HTML part, addressed to the account's own email address and never to an address taken from a request. No QR code, no barcode, no image, no attachment, no card data and no token that signs anybody in.
AcceptanceCriteria: For booking FR-ABCD-EFGH, three Premium seats inserted in the order F9, F7, F8 in Hall 3, showtime stored `2026-08-21T13:45:00Z`, total `84372` paise and `PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://example.invalid`, the plain-text part equals the block published verbatim under Copy in `docs/03 PRD/sections/E4_receipt_entry.md`, compared BYTE FOR BYTE with LF line endings and explicitly NOT whitespace-collapsed: the 5 blank lines must be present in their published positions and each label line must carry its exact run of spaces, `Film` `Hall` and `Paid` each followed by 6 spaces, `Showtime` by 2 and `Seats` by 5, so that every value begins at column 11; the 15 lines in order are `Your booking is confirmed.`, blank, `Booking reference: FR-ABCD-EFGH`, blank, `Film      DEMO MOVIE 01`, `Hall      Hall 3`, `Showtime  21 Aug 2026, 7:15 pm (Asia/Kolkata)`, `Seats     F7, F8, F9`, `Paid      Rs 843.72`, blank, `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`, blank, `You can see this booking again at https://example.invalid/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH`, blank, `This booking is final. There is no cancellation and no refund.`; the subject equals `Your FrontRow booking FR-ABCD-EFGH`; the HTML part contains `₹843.72` while the plain-text part contains `Rs 843.72` and zero occurrences of `₹`, carries the anchor text `See this booking again`, has exactly one `href=` attribute whose value equals `https://example.invalid/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH`, and contains zero occurrences of each of `<img`, `<table` and `<td`; the message has 0 attachments and no part whose content type begins `image/`; a resend renders a body byte-identical to the first send; every rendered field is read from PostgreSQL at send time and none from the queue payload, asserted by UPDATEing the film title between the enqueue and the send and finding the new title in the sent body.
