Title: Re-send a receipt on the owner's request, and refuse without cost when there is nothing to send
Description: The booking's owner, and nobody else with no role exempt, can re-enqueue their receipt: the request raises dispatch_seq and inserts one outbox row in one transaction, or refuses. It is a convenience for a customer who deleted the email and is not the answer to SES failing, because a customer who never received anything may not know to look.
AcceptanceCriteria: `POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-EFGH/resend-receipt` as the owner against a `sent` row returns 202 with body keys exactly `queued, email_address`, `queued` true and `email_address` equal to the account address, and `SELECT dispatch_seq, status FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` moves from `1, sent` to `2, pending` with exactly one new outbox_message carrying dispatch_seq 2; against a `pending` row with attempts 0 it returns 202 with `queued` false, inserts no outbox row, leaves dispatch_seq at 1 and spends no rate-limit token, proved by an immediately following resend being accepted once the row reaches `sent`; against `sending`, and against `pending` with attempts above 0, it returns 202 `queued` false and inserts nothing; against a `suppressed` row it returns 409 RECEIPT_SUPPRESSED on the first call and on the hundredth, spends no token, and changes no column, asserted by SELECTing every column of that receipt_dispatch row before and after and comparing the tuples; as a signed-in non-owner, including an admin, it returns 404 whose parsed body, with error.request_id deleted, equals the unknown-reference 404's parsed body with that same field deleted - the envelope carries one on every error and it is unique per request; `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log` is unchanged on every branch; a queued message still carrying dispatch_seq 1 after the row reached 2 produces 0 SES calls.
SourceRef: P-TKT-07 EP-TKT-02 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-067

Title: Rate limit the reference lookup and the resend, failing closed
Description: Three limiters guard this lane: a per-user and a per-IP lookup bucket shared by both endpoints, and a per-booking resend interval of RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (300, ASSUMED). Retry-After carries whichever one refused and is derived, never typed. It sits in phase 7 because phase 7 delivers rate limiting.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `RATE_LIMIT_LOOKUP_USER_PER_MIN=20`, the 21st `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` from one user inside one injected-clock minute returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with header `Retry-After: 3`, which equals ceil(60/20), and the rendered copy is `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.`; with `RATE_LIMIT_LOOKUP_IP_PER_MIN=60`, the 61st request from one address across different user accounts returns `Retry-After: 1` and the copy is `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` with the singular noun; with `RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300`, a second resend 60 injected seconds after an accepted one returns 429 with `Retry-After: 240` and the copy `A receipt was requested recently. You can request another in 4 minutes.`, and at 250 injected seconds elapsed the header reads 50 and the copy renders seconds - every injected advance in this criterion is honoured by the Redis test double the harness supplies, whose key expiry and TTL reads are driven by the same injected clock, because real Redis expires its own keys on wall time and would report 300 at both points; with Redis unreachable both endpoints return 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and the PostgreSQL query counter for the request is 0, so no fallback occurs; no Retry-After figure appears as a literal inside any copy string: driving the same component with a response carrying `Retry-After: 7` renders `Too many attempts. Try again in 7 seconds.`, and `rg -nF -e 'in 3 seconds' -e 'in 1 second' -e 'in 4 minutes' frontend/src` returns 0 hits.
SourceRef: P-TKT-02 P-TKT-07 P-TKT-09 FR-ADR-058 EP-TKT-01 EP-TKT-02

Title: Build nothing for the door, and prove nothing was built
Description: Entry is a person at the entrance reading the reference and checking it by hand: no scanner, no validation endpoint, no door screen, no staff account and no state anywhere marking a reference as used. OPEN-DOORVERIFY-01 - the venue cannot tell a real reference from an invented one, because no surface returns a booking to anyone but its owner - and OPEN-DUPREF-01 - who is admitted when one reference is presented twice - are both open, and this story invents neither a door surface nor an admission policy.
AcceptanceCriteria: Loading `docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json` and testing every `endpoints[].path`, no path contains any of `/validate`, `/scan`, `/checkin`, `/check-in`, `/door`, `/admit` or `/tickets`, and exactly 2 endpoints have a path beginning `/api/bookings/by-reference/` - EP-TKT-01 and EP-TKT-02 - whose `authorisation_rule` strings each contain the literal `user_id equals their own user id`; `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='booking' AND column_name IN ('used_at','admitted_at','scanned_at','checked_in_at','entry_at')` returns 0; presenting one reference twice writes nothing, asserted by running `SELECT count(*)` over every table in `information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public'` before and after two consecutive owner `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-EFGH` calls and finding every count identical, audit_log among them; SCR-TKT-01 and the plain-text part of SCR-TKT-02 each render the line `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`; no QR code, barcode or image is produced anywhere, asserted by `python -m pip freeze` in the built backend image listing none of the distributions `qrcode`, `segno`, `pyqrcode`, `python-barcode`, `treepoem`, `pyzbar` or `reportlab`, by no endpoint in contract.json declaring a response content type beginning `image/`, and by the sent receipt message having 0 attachments and no part whose content type begins `image/`.
SourceRef: P-TKT-08 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02 SRC-001 §E E-9 SRC-002 §E E-5

Title: Keep the receipt's dispatch state off the customer API and write no message for a failed send
Description: OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01 is open and reserved to the client: what a customer is told when a receipt definitively fails, and whether the booking stays valid, is not decided here. Phase 5 ships the mechanism and not the message, and no operator action on a failed receipt is built either, because an administrative action taken on a customer's booking after a post-capture send failure is the substance of that row.
AcceptanceCriteria: For two bookings identical except that one receipt_dispatch row reads `sent` and the other `failed`, `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` returns bodies that differ only in the reference value, and SCR-TKT-01 renders DOM that differs only in the reference and the booking facts, so queued, in flight, sent and failed are indistinguishable on the customer API; a failed send changes no column on the booking row, asserted by SELECTing every column of that row before the worker marks the dispatch row failed and comparing the tuples after; `docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json` contains exactly one endpoint whose path ends `/resend-receipt`, its `authorisation_rule` contains the literal `user_id equals their own user id`, and no endpoint path in the contract contains `/cancel` or `/refund`; `rg -in -e sns -e bounce -e complaint -e SetIdentity backend/app` returns 0 hits and `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND column_name IN ('email_invalid','email_bounced','email_complained','email_suppressed')` returns 0; `rg -n 'cancelled_at' backend/app/api backend/app/domain backend/app/workers` returns 0 hits, so the column exists only in the model layer and nothing reads or writes it; and no customer-facing string reports a failed receipt, asserted by `rg -inF -e 'receipt failed' -e 'could not be sent' -e 'was not sent' -e 'undelivered' -e 'not delivered' -e 'delivery failed' -e 'bounced' -e 'is delayed' -e 'still sending' frontend/src` returning 0 hits over that closed string set.
SourceRef: P-TKT-10 P-TKT-11 P-TKT-09 FR-ADR-049 FR-ADR-060

Title: Say in the runbook that sent means SES accepted, never that the customer received
Description: receipt_dispatch records SES acceptance only; bounces and complaints publish to SNS and nothing subscribes, so a bounced or spam-filed receipt sits in the table as sent and is indistinguishable from one that reached the inbox. Dead letter queue depth is not alarmed, outbox pending count is not alarmed, the SES bounce rate is not alarmed, and /metrics is not scraped - the runbook must say all of it in these terms, because the short version is the one that ends a support conversation wrongly.
AcceptanceCriteria: The phase 7 runbook, at `docs/35 Hypercare/runbook.md` (SRC-002 §12.8's filename, relocated to that folder by FR-ADR-008), exists and carries a heading containing `Receipt`; within that file each of the literal strings `evidence of dispatch, never of receipt`, `depth is not alarmed`, `nothing scrapes it`, `indistinguishable from one that reached the inbox`, `running task count below 1`, `dead letter queue depth`, `outbox_message pending count`, `SES bounce and complaint rate`, `no endpoint, screen or job in v1 re-sends a receipt on an operator's behalf` and `a dead letter redrive is a Zone C console action` appears at least once, `rg -c` returning 1 or more for each; the file carries two fenced `sql` blocks, one containing both `FROM receipt_dispatch` and `GROUP BY status` and one containing both `FROM outbox_message` and `status = 'pending'`; and `rg -inF -e 'means the customer received' -e 'confirms delivery' -e 'proves delivery' -e 'the receipt was delivered' -e 'the customer has received' -e 'confirms the customer got' -e 'the receipt reached' 'docs/35 Hypercare/runbook.md'` returns 0 hits over that closed string set.
SourceRef: P-TKT-11 FR-ADR-068 FR-ADR-060 FR-ADR-057 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-01

Title: Send the password-reset email exactly once per request
Description: The same outbox, the same relay, the same worker and the same SES port carry the account lane's reset email, so it is specified to the same standard as the receipt rather than left as a branch. The token row is the claim and it carries the stale branch, because a worker that dies between the claim and the send must not cost a locked-out customer the only route back into their account, and the token value never travels in the queue.
AcceptanceCriteria: Delivering the same password_reset.send message twice produces exactly 1 SES call and `SELECT email_claimed_at IS NOT NULL, email_sent_at IS NOT NULL FROM password_reset_token WHERE id=:t` reads `true, true`; with the worker killed after the claim and before the send the row reads email_claimed_at set and email_sent_at null, and - email_claimed_at being written from the injected clock and the staleness threshold bound from that same clock, exactly as S-TKT-07 requires of receipt_dispatch.claimed_at - a redelivery at claim plus 120 injected seconds makes 0 SES calls and deletes the message, while a redelivery at claim plus 901 injected seconds with `RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS=900` reclaims the row and makes exactly 1 SES call; an SES refusal, and a call abandoned at SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS, each set email_claimed_at back to null, leave email_sent_at null and do not delete the queue message; a redelivery arriving 24 injected hours after email_sent_at was set makes 0 SES calls, because email_sent_at is never cleared; the enqueued payload key set is exactly `message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id` and, with the token generator stubbed to return `TESTTOKENVALUE0001`, `rg -F 'TESTTOKENVALUE0001'` over the raw enqueued message body returns 0 hits; the worker's booking-resolution deletion rule is not applied to this topic, asserted by a password_reset.send message surviving a worker in which every booking lookup fails.
SourceRef: P-TKT-12 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-059

Title: Hold the cross-cutting floors every other lane is built on
Description: Everything that is true on every request, every screen and every process, and that no single feature owns: the two-layer seat guarantee, integer money, the audit row, authorisation on the router, credentials and sessions, the rate limiter, the cache, health and readiness, logging, configuration, secrets, shutdown, statelessness, migrations, backups, the memory budget, accessibility, the zone boundary, scope governance and the seed. Each of these is a defect a customer eventually meets, and each has a wrong implementation that passes ordinary tests.

Title: Prove no seat is sold twice under fifty simultaneous hold requests
Description: The product's central invariant, proved rather than asserted (SRC-001 §3.2). This is Stage A of the drill: the fifty-request gate at the hold endpoint. It proves the Redis lock layer and the end-to-end result, and it is recorded as exercising the unique constraint zero times, which is why Stage B (S-XCT-02) exists and may not be skipped. This gate is never waived, never skipped and never marked expected-to-fail.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/stress_seats.py --base-url http://localhost:8000 --showtime 41 --seat 312 --n 50 run against the local compose stack reports exactly 1 HTTP 201 and exactly 49 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE - exactly one, never 'at most one', and zero winners is also a failure; the winner then confirms and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312 read directly from PostgreSQL returns exactly 1; the script records the start instant of each of the fifty requests and asserts the spread between first and last is under STRESS_CONCURRENCY_SPREAD_MS (default 100 ms), exiting non-zero and printing the literal line NOT CONCURRENT: spread {n} ms exceeds {limit} ms rather than 'passed' when it is not; the run reports unique_constraint_violations = 0, because all 49 losers are refused by Redis at SET ... NX and the constraint is never reached at the hold endpoint; the run reports distinct_users = 50, the fifty sessions coming from S-XCT-17's warm-up, and exits non-zero when it is fewer; rg -n 'RATE_LIMIT' scripts/stress_seats.py returns only the two read-and-print lines S-XCT-17 specifies and no assignment, so the script cannot raise, lower or disable a bucket; rg -nP 'localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|https?://' scripts/stress_seats.py returns hits only on the default value of --base-url, so the deployed run differs from the local run by that one argument and nothing else; the script prints its outcome as one JSON object on stdout carrying operator, run_at as an ISO-8601 UTC instant, base_url, winners, losers, spread_ms, distinct_users and unique_constraint_violations, reads operator from STRESS_OPERATOR which has no default, and exits non-zero naming STRESS_OPERATOR when it is unset, because an unattributed undated claim that it was run is not evidence.

Title: Watch the unique constraint fail and work again with two live holders on one seat
Description: Stage B of the red-proof drill, added on 2026-08-22 because the single-stage drill could not work: the fifty-request gate fires at the hold, where the constraint is never reached, so dropping it changed nothing and the never-waivable gate reported failure against a correct implementation. Stage B produces the only state from which two confirms both reach the insert. Nothing is disabled - a lock key is made to disappear, which is a fault the database half exists to survive.
AcceptanceCriteria: With PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS=1500 in the local compose stack: customer A holds seat (41, 312) and issues a confirm asynchronously; inside that delay window the drill runs DEL lock:seat:41:312 directly in Redis; customer B then holds the same seat and receives 201 with token tB, because SET ... NX succeeds on the missing key and no committed booking_seat row exists yet - two live holders on one seat; B confirms and both transactions reach the seat-occupancy insert. COUNTS BELOW ARE OVER THE TWO CONFIRM RESPONSES ONLY - the two holds also return 201 and are setup, not the measured population. With the constraint present the two confirms produce exactly 1 HTTP 201, exactly 1 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and exactly 1 booking_seat row for (41, 312), and that 409 is the constraint firing, observed. The constraint is then dropped with ALTER TABLE booking_seat DROP CONSTRAINT and the steps repeated: the two confirms produce exactly 2 HTTP 201s and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312 returns exactly 2 - the seat sold twice. If it still returns 1 the script exits non-zero printing the literal line DRILL VOID: constraint dropped and count(*) is 1, and the story is marked Blocked. The constraint is restored, the repeat produces exactly 1 row again, and SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returns exactly one row whose definition is UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) with no WHERE clause. Stage A - which is S-XCT-01's separate fifty-request run against the HOLD endpoint, not any part of this story - produces one winner even with the constraint dropped, and that is the expected result and not a finding, because at the hold endpoint the Redis lock decides and the constraint is never reached. That is the whole reason this story exists. The script refuses to run when --base-url does not resolve to a loopback address, exiting non-zero with LOCAL ONLY; each stage prints one JSON object on stdout carrying operator (from STRESS_OPERATOR, no default, exit non-zero when unset), run_at, stage and every count above.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 FR-ADR-024 E8 S7.1

Title: Enforce the seat guarantee in two independent systems and waive neither half
Description: A Redis lock provides the hold and a unique constraint plus row locking provides the truth. The database half may not be waived at any confidence for any reason - waiving a quality check is reserved to the client, and this is the check. The two layers catch different events: the lock refuses a second customer while a first holds the seat, the constraint refuses a second confirm after Redis was wrong. Why there is no pre-insert check: a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is a row lock, and a row lock on rows that do not exist locks nothing, so two transactions would both find no seat row and both insert. The constraint is the only thing between them.
AcceptanceCriteria: A total UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) constraint exists on the seat-occupancy table with no WHERE clause, verified by SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returning exactly one row whose definition contains no WHERE; rg -n 'ON CONFLICT' backend/app returns 0 hits; rg -n 'FOR UPDATE' backend/app | rg -v 'FROM showtime' returns 0 hits, so every row lock in the application is taken on the showtime row and none on a seat-occupancy row that does not exist yet; the confirm path performs no pre-insert availability check, observed rather than grepped - S-XCT-02's dropped-constraint run produces 2 rows, which a pre-insert check would have reduced to 1 by returning 409 before the insert; a unique violation at insert is caught and returned as HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, never HTTP 500, is not retried, and is logged at INFO with the seat_conflicts_total counter incremented rather than as an exception; the body of that 409 carries message 'C12 was taken by another customer before your payment finished. Your booking was not made and you have not been charged.' when one seat was lost and 'C12 and C13 were taken by another customer before your payment finished. Your booking was not made and you have not been charged.' when two or more were (P-HLD-14 rows 4 and 4b), asserted byte-for-byte on both, and this floor publishes no sentence of its own; SHOW transaction_isolation issued inside the confirm transaction returns read committed, and the two-holder drill of S-XCT-02 is run at that level.

Title: Create the seat-occupancy unique constraint in the Phase 2 migration
Description: The constraint is created before any code can write a booking, so no window exists in which bookings are written without it. Removing it is a schema change and the only permitted removal is the local red-proof drill.
AcceptanceCriteria: The Alembic revision that creates the seat-occupancy table creates UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) in the same revision, verified by running alembic upgrade head against an empty database and then SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returning exactly one row; the create_table and the unique constraint carry the same revision id, asserted by rg -l "create_table\('booking_seat'" backend/migrations/versions and rg -l "'showtime_id', 'seat_id'" backend/migrations/versions returning the same single file, so no earlier revision can have written a seat row without the constraint in place; rg -in 'drop_constraint|DROP CONSTRAINT' backend/migrations returns 0 hits, so no later revision up to head removes it; the definition read back from pg_get_constraintdef contains no WHERE clause and the constraint is a constraint rather than a partial index, asserted by SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'booking_seat' containing no WHERE.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 P-XCT-19 FR-ADR-062 E8 S7.1 E8 S7.18

Title: Compute and store every money value as integer paise through one function
Description: Currency is INR, the minor unit is paise and the ratio is 100. Decimal at the parsing boundary, bigint in persistence, a formatted string at render time only. Changing CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO is a one-way door reserved to the client: bookings are permanent, and no row records which interpretation it was written under.
AcceptanceCriteria: CURRENCY_CODE=INR and CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO=100 are loaded and validated at boot and logged once, and the process exits non-zero at boot if the ratio is anything other than 100 while the code is INR; every money column is bigint and every money identifier carries a _paise suffix, asserted by SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND column_name ~ '(price|amount|total)' AND (data_type <> 'bigint' OR column_name NOT LIKE '%\_paise') returning 0 rows; rg -nP 'float\(|:\s*float|->\s*float' backend/app returns 0 hits; backend/app/domain/pricing.py defines exactly one public function, seat_price_paise(base_price_paise: int, uplift_basis_points: int) -> int, and rg -n 'uplift_basis_points' backend/app scripts --glob '!**/domain/pricing.py' --glob '!**/models/**' --glob '!**/migrations/**' returns 0 hits, so the formula is written once and nowhere else; rg -l 'from app.domain.pricing import seat_price_paise' backend/app scripts returns exactly five files - the seat-map read, the checkout total, the receipt render, the dashboard query and scripts/seed.py; the stated fixture, base_price_paise 25000 at a Recliner uplift of 3333 basis points, gives 25000 * (10000 + 3333) / 10000 = 33332.5, rounded half-up to 33333, and three such seats produce a booking total of exactly 99999 paise and never 99998, because the total is the sum of already-rounded per-seat prices and the total is never rounded; POST /api/admin/showtimes with body {"movie_id": 1, "screen_id": 1, "starts_at": "2026-09-01T18:00:00", "ends_at": "2026-09-01T20:30:00", "base_price_paise": 250.00} returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and the value is rejected and never rounded, and the same body with base_price_paise -1 and with base_price_paise 0 each returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, and the same three cases on PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/41 return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; SELECT SUM(price_paise) over a bigint money column is cast back to BigInteger in the query and the value arriving in Python satisfies isinstance(value, int) and never isinstance(value, Decimal).
SourceRef: P-XCT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-038 E8 S7.2

Title: Write every privileged change and its audit row in one transaction
Description: Either both land or neither does. An audit row written after the commit is missing exactly the rows that crashed. The rows are written from Phase 2 even though the screen that reads them is Phase 8, because an audit trail that starts when its reader is built has a hole exactly as long as the build took.
AcceptanceCriteria: An admin changing showtime 41's base price from 25000 to 28000 paise during request {request_id} commits one audit_log row in the same transaction as the change, carrying actor_user_id 17, actor_role admin, action showtime.base_price_changed, entity_type showtime, entity_id 41, before {"base_price_paise": 25000}, after {"base_price_paise": 28000} and request_id {request_id}; with the audit-insert call patched to raise RuntimeError the whole transaction rolls back, SELECT base_price_paise FROM showtime WHERE id = 41 still returns 25000 and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log returns its pre-request value; with the showtime UPDATE patched to raise, SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE entity_id = 41 AND action = 'showtime.base_price_changed' returns 0; actor_user_id is NOT NULL and carries a foreign key to users(id), asserted by SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='audit_log' AND column_name='actor_user_id' returning NO and by SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='audit_log'::regclass AND contype='f' returning one row for it; actor_role is copied at the time of the write and never resolved by a join at read time, asserted by updating user 17's role to manager after the write and re-reading the same audit_log row, whose actor_role still reads admin; SELECT count(*) FROM jsonb_object_keys(before) and the same over after each return 1 for this change, so neither carries a whole-row snapshot, and before IS NULL for a creation; SELECT data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name='audit_log' AND column_name='occurred_at' returns 'timestamp with time zone', and the value the application binds for occurred_at is an aware datetime whose utcoffset() is zero, asserted by a SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener capturing the bound parameter for that INSERT. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.
SourceRef: P-XCT-03 SRC-001 §7.6 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-012 E8 S7.3

Title: Make audit_log append-only in the database and close the action vocabulary
Description: Append-only at the database-role level rather than by convention, and a closed controlled vocabulary for action - because a filter written against a non-member returns an empty list while looking entirely correct.
AcceptanceCriteria: The application database role holds INSERT and SELECT on audit_log and no UPDATE and no DELETE, verified by SELECT privilege_type FROM information_schema.table_privileges WHERE table_name = 'audit_log' AND grantee = current_user returning exactly the two rows INSERT and SELECT; UPDATE audit_log SET action = 'x' issued as that role raises a permission error, the request returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and the response body's message is exactly 'The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote {request_id}.' with no variant minted for the audit path; DELETE FROM audit_log as that role raises the same permission error and returns the same body; the closed vocabulary is the module-level tuple AUDIT_ACTIONS in backend/app/domain/audit.py, and a value outside it is refused with 500 INTERNAL_ERROR at a boundary check that runs before the transaction opens, asserted by a test in which the shortened paraphrase base_price_changed is refused and showtime.base_price_changed is accepted and by SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE id = 41 AND base_price_paise = 28000 returning 0 after the refusal; every action literal in the application is a member of that tuple, asserted by a test that collects rg -noP "action=['\"][a-z0-9_.]+['\"]" backend/app and finds every captured value in AUDIT_ACTIONS. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.
SourceRef: P-XCT-03 FR-ADR-019 E8 S7.3

Title: Answer who booked any seat, when, and what they paid
Description: Answered by the permanent booking record and not by the audit log: a customer booking a seat is the product working, not a privileged write. Rendered in Asia/Kolkata, because the date boundary is taken in the cinema's zone and never in the container's UTC.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/seats/312?showtime_id=41 as an admin returns 200, and the same answer is read back with SELECT b.id, b.user_id, b.created_at, bs.price_paise FROM booking_seat bs JOIN booking b ON b.id = bs.booking_id WHERE bs.showtime_id = 41 AND bs.seat_id = 312, which returns exactly one row: booking_id 9008, user_id 4471, created_at 2026-08-12T18:41:03Z and price_paise 28124 - the seeded base of 24999 paise at the Premium uplift of 1250 basis points, 24999 * 11250 / 10000 = 28123.875 rounded half-up, snapshotted at hold acquisition and never recomputed, asserted by changing the showtime's base price afterwards and re-reading the same 28124; the response renders the text 'Booked by customer-07@demo.frontrow.invalid on 13 Aug 2026 at 00:11 (Asia/Kolkata) for ₹281.24' - 18:41:03Z on 12 August is 00:11 on 13 August in Asia/Kolkata, so the rendered date is the local one and not the container's UTC; the same SELECT can never return two rows, guaranteed by the unique constraint of S-XCT-03, and returning zero rows gives HTTP 200 with an empty result and the rendered text 'This seat has not been booked.', which is a valid answer and not an error; the same request as manager 88, who is assigned screens 2 and 5, returns 200 with a non-empty result when seat 312 is on screen 2 and 403 FORBIDDEN with message 'This account does not have access to that hall.' when it is on screen 4 - the mandated test asserts both halves, because a test asserting only 'denied' passes against a query that returns nothing for anybody; GET /api/bookings/9008 as a customer who is not user 4471 returns 403 FORBIDDEN.
SourceRef: P-XCT-04 SRC-001 §7.6 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-039 E8 S7.19

Title: Make nothing on a path to a booking deletable
Description: The question 'who booked this seat and when' has to be answerable at any time, which means nothing on a path that can reach a booking is ever removed. The product is not delete-free in general - a seat and a manager screen assignment are genuinely deleted - and those two are unreachable from a booking by their own preconditions. Note for the implementer, not an acceptance criterion: tables that are edited after creation are expected to carry updated_at as well as created_at; which tables those are is a judgement that follows from the data model and is checked there rather than here.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every foreign key on a path that can reach a booking is declared ON DELETE RESTRICT and none is CASCADE or SET NULL, verified by SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = 'f' AND confdeltype <> 'r' returning 0 rows; booking.user_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, read back from pg_constraint and information_schema.columns; DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 4471 with a booking present fails with SQLSTATE 23503 rather than succeeding silently; rg -in 'DELETE FROM (booking|booking_seat|payment|audit_log|users|showtime|movie)' backend/app backend/migrations returns 0 hits, so no code path prunes a table on that path, and no retention window or scheduled deletion exists anywhere, which S-XCT-36's scheduler assertions carry; SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables t WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name NOT IN ('alembic_version', 'audit_log') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns c WHERE c.table_name = t.table_name AND c.column_name = 'created_at') returns 0 rows; exactly two entities are ever removed from the database - a seat, through DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} (EP-ADM-21), permitted only while its hall has no showtime rows at all, and a manager_screen_assignment row, removed by PUT /api/admin/managers/{user_id}/screens (EP-ADM-24) replacing the whole set - and neither is reachable from a booking by its own preconditions; walking the mounted route table returns exactly three DELETE routes, /api/admin/seats/{seat_id}, /api/holds/{hold_token}/seats/{seat_id} and /api/holds/{hold_token}, and the last two release Redis keys and delete no database row, asserted by comparing every table's row count before and after each.
SourceRef: P-XCT-04 P-XCT-22 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02

Title: Apply authorisation once, on each of the four routers, as a dependency
Description: Four routers - public, customer, reporting and admin - each with one authorisation dependency. A handler contains no role check, because a per-handler check is the pattern that eventually misses one. PROVISIONAL: the four-role set is a build-session reading of SRC-003 C-1 and one message from the client reverses it; the story is written against the reading recorded there and decides nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: Four routers exist and each carries exactly one authorisation dependency attached at the router: public (no session), customer (/api/me, /api/bookings, /api/holds), reporting (/api/reports, role manager or admin) and admin (/api/admin, role admin only), asserted by walking app.routes and finding that every APIRoute's dependant carries the router-level dependency for its prefix - include_router() FLATTENS routers into the application, so app.routes holds APIRoute objects and NEVER an APIRouter, and a correct four-router build yields zero APIRouter instances; rg -nP "role\s*==|role\s*!=|current_user\.role|require_role|\.role\b" backend/app/api/routes returns 0 hits, every authorisation dependency living in backend/app/api/deps.py; the caller's role is read from the user row on every request and never from a claim in the token, asserted by a test that updates users.role in the database and observes the new role take effect on the very next request with the same unchanged cookie, rather than at the next sign-in; a request with no session to a non-public router returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; a session whose JWT is expired or does not verify returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with message 'You were signed out. Sign in again to continue.'; a signed-in user reaching a router their role does not permit returns 403 FORBIDDEN; PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/101 as a manager returns 403 FORBIDDEN refused by the admin router's role dependency before the body is parsed, asserted by sending a body that would itself fail validation and still receiving 403 and not 422, and this case carries its own test because it is the one SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 exists to prevent; the reporting router mounts no route whose method is POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, asserted by walking the route table.
SourceRef: P-XCT-05 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-003 C-1 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-009 FR-ADR-011 S3 S3.5

Title: Resolve a manager's screen scope from the session and never from the request
Description: A screen id in the query string may only narrow the set the dependency resolved and can never widen it. A handler that read screen_id and trusted it would hand a manager a hall they are not assigned to. Sits at Phase 8 because the reporting surface it asserts against is Phase 8; the dependency itself ships with the router at Phase 2 (S-XCT-10).
AcceptanceCriteria: With manager 88 assigned screens 2 and 5: GET /api/reports/dashboard with no screen_id returns 200 with a non-empty body covering exactly screens 2 and 5, resolved from the session; GET /api/reports/dashboard?screen_id=2 returns 200 non-empty; GET /api/reports/dashboard?screen_id=4 returns 403 FORBIDDEN and is refused rather than honoured; POST /api/reports/dashboard returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED in the product envelope and not 404, because the path exists for GET; the scope is applied in the query's WHERE clause by the dependency and never by filtering rows after they are fetched, asserted by capturing the emitted SQL with a SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener and finding the statement's parameters carry exactly (2, 5) for the screen_id binding - before_cursor_execute receives PARAMETERISED sql with the values in a separate argument, so the literal never appears in the statement text, and by rg -nP 'if .*screen_id|filter\(lambda' backend/app/api/routes/reports.py returning 0 hits; the mandated test asserts both halves - a non-empty, non-zero figure for the manager's own screen and a denied result for another's - because a test asserting only 'denied' passes against a query that returns nothing for anybody; a manager with no screens assigned receives 200 and an empty dashboard, which is the correct state for a new account and must not render as an error; an admin runs the same three requests with no screen filter and receives 200 in every case, including screen_id=4.
SourceRef: P-XCT-05 SRC-001 §4.4 SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 FR-ADR-011 S3 S3.4

Title: Store credentials so they cannot be read back
Description: Our own email and password with bcrypt, off the event loop. Never Cognito. The 72-byte ceiling is enforced explicitly with its own message because bcrypt silently truncates there, and a truncation nobody sees means two different long passwords authenticate the same account.
AcceptanceCriteria: Registration with an 11-character password returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with message 'Use a password of at least 12 characters.', the floor being PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH characters and not bytes; 25 Devanagari characters, which are 75 bytes, return 422 with 'Use a password of 72 bytes or fewer. Some characters count as more than one byte.' and are not silently truncated, while 72 Latin characters are accepted; a second registration at an address already registered returns 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED and not a generic 422, so the interface can offer the sign-in tab and the reset link; a wrong email or password at sign-in returns 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID and not AUTH_REQUIRED; a unique index exists on lower(email), asserted by SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'users' returning one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX containing lower(email), and the email is stored as entered, asserted by registering Nikhil@Example.invalid and reading the column back unchanged; a 255-character email returns 422 and a 254-character one is accepted; rg -nP 'bcrypt\.(hashpw|checkpw|gensalt)' backend/app --glob '!**/core/security.py' returns 0 hits and rg -n 'async def' backend/app/core/security.py returns 0 hits, so no bcrypt call can run on the event loop, and rg -c 'to_thread.run_sync' backend/app/api/routes/auth.py returns at least 1; sign-in against an unknown email calls the same verify function against a dummy hash, asserted by patching it and observing exactly one call for both a known and an unknown address; a registration made with the password Correct-Horse-99! produces no captured stdout line containing that string, no response body containing it, and SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'users' AND column_name IN ('password', 'password_plain') returns 0 rows.

Title: Carry the session in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie with Secure from configuration
Description: SameSite=Lax is this product's only cross-site request defence - there is no CSRF token, no double-submit cookie and no Origin check anywhere - so the two changes that remove it are named and tested against. Touches OPEN-TLS-01, which is OPEN and DEFERRED: the criterion specifies only the surface the deferral forces and says nothing about whether TLS is or will be terminated anywhere.
AcceptanceCriteria: A successful sign-in sets the session cookie with HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and Max-Age equal to SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (43200), and with Secure present if and only if COOKIE_SECURE is true, asserted by parsing the Set-Cookie header on both settings; COOKIE_SECURE has no default and the process exits non-zero at boot printing a message naming COOKIE_SECURE when it is absent; a boot-time cross-field check refuses COOKIE_SECURE=true unless PUBLIC_BASE_URL begins with https:// and the process exits non-zero naming both variables; rg -n 'localStorage' frontend/src returns 0 hits; no endpoint in the product changes state on a GET, asserted by a test that walks the mounted route table, issues every GET route inside one transaction and reads SELECT sum(n_tup_ins + n_tup_upd + n_tup_del) FROM pg_stat_xact_user_tables, which returns 0 - this is a stated security requirement and not REST tidiness, because Lax sends the cookie on a top-level GET navigation; rg -in 'samesite=none|samesite: *.none.' backend/app frontend/src returns 0 hits, the scan scoped to the two application trees and never to the repository root because this criterion quotes the pattern it searches for and a root-wide run matches its own text in docs/05 Bible/; a session that expires mid-flow returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED and the seat selection is still readable from the browser's sessionStorage afterwards, asserted by reading sessionStorage.getItem('fr.selection') - the per-change selection key owned by P-SEA-03, not the one-shot fr.pending_selection of P-ACC-13 - and finding its parsed seat ids are exactly C12 and C13, the two selected before the expiry.
SourceRef: P-XCT-06 P-XCT-29 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01 FR-ADR-069 E8 S7.5

Title: Rate-limit per user and per IP with one atomic Redis token bucket that fails closed
Description: A token bucket evaluated by a Lua script so the read, the refill and the decrement are one atomic operation, two independent buckets per limited request, and 503 rather than unlimited access when Redis is gone. Bucket values are estimates, not measurements, and Phase 7's load test replaces them.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each limited request evaluates two buckets - one keyed on the server-derived user id, one on the resolved client address - inside a single Lua script invocation, and both must have a token for the request to proceed, asserted twice: with RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_USER_PER_MIN=1 and RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN=100 one customer's second POST /api/showtimes/41/holds returns 429 while a second customer's first from the same address returns 201, and with the two values swapped two different customers from one address exhaust the IP bucket and the second receives 429; an empty bucket returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header in integer seconds and details.retry_after_seconds equal to it; with the Redis container stopped POST /api/showtimes/41/holds returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with message 'Seat holds are unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.' and never 200, asserted by stopping Redis and issuing one limited request; a retry carrying an already-seen Idempotency-Key still consumes a token, asserted by exhausting a bucket with repeats of one key; every bucket size is a named configuration variable and no bucket size is a literal, asserted by rg -nP '(?<![\w.])[2-9]\d*(?![\w.])' backend/app/core/ratelimit.py backend/app/core/ratelimit.lua returning 0 hits and by rg -c 'RATE_LIMIT_' backend/app/core/config.py returning one declaration per bucket in S7.20's table; FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS set to * exits non-zero at boot naming the variable; with Redis stopped the refused request issues exactly one Redis command, asserted by a counting client wrapper, so the failure path reads nothing further from Redis to build its error message or its log line.

Title: Take the real client address from the right of X-Forwarded-For
Description: A rate limiter behind a load balancer limits the load balancer. This has a wrong implementation that is silent - trusting the leftmost entry, which a client can forge - so it carries its own test rather than relying on the limiter's own tests passing.
AcceptanceCriteria: The limiter keys on the address the load balancer reports and not on the load balancer itself, proved as its own test rather than inferred from the limiter's tests passing. With RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN=2 and the local proxy configured to append the peer address to X-Forwarded-For exactly as an ALB does, three POST /api/showtimes/41/holds requests arrive from one simulated client 198.51.100.77 for three different seats: the first carries X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9 and reaches the application as '203.0.113.9, 198.51.100.77', the second carries X-Forwarded-For: 192.0.2.5 and reaches it as '192.0.2.5, 198.51.100.77', and the third carries no such header and reaches it as '198.51.100.77'. The first two return 201 and the third returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with header Retry-After: 30 and body message 'Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.' - all three were counted in one bucket, and two forged leftmost values changed nothing. Against an implementation that trusts the leftmost entry the third request returns 201 and the test fails. The resolved address is 198.51.100.77 in all three cases, read back from the request log line's client_ip field. The application runs with --proxy-headers and an explicit --forwarded-allow-ips, asserted by rg -n 'proxy-headers' and rg -n 'forwarded-allow-ips' over the entrypoint returning one hit each, and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS = * exits non-zero at boot naming the variable. Nothing client-supplied selects a bucket key: with RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN=1, a second request carrying header X-RateLimit-Key: other, query string ?bucket=other and body field bucket 'other' still returns 429, and the two keys the Lua script is invoked with for that request are exactly rl:hold:user:4471 and rl:hold:ip:198.51.100.77 for signed-in customer 4471, compared as literal strings, every key matching ^rl:[a-z][a-z_]*:(user|ip):[0-9a-zA-Z.:_-]+$ - bucket name, then dimension, then identifier - the bucket-name segment being required and not optional, because the six buckets S7.20 tabulates cannot share one key without the sign-in bucket spending the seat-hold bucket's tokens.

Title: Compute Retry-After from the bucket's refill rate and never from a constant
Description: 900 was published once as a wait, and 900 is the sign-in bucket's window rather than its refill interval. Every derivation is tabulated once in S7.20 and the header is computed at the point of refusal.
AcceptanceCriteria: Retry-After is ceil(window_seconds / capacity) for the bucket that actually refused, computed and never typed, and every figure below is the one S7.20 tabulates: the seat-hold per-user bucket at 20 tokens per 60 s gives ceil(60/20) = 3, the header reads Retry-After: 3 and the message is 'Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.'; the seat-hold per-IP bucket at 60 per 60 s gives ceil(60/60) = 1 and the message is 'Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.', singular; the sign-in per-IP bucket at 30 per 900 s gives ceil(900/30) = 30 and reads 'Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.'; the sign-in per-user bucket at 10 per 900 s gives ceil(900/10) = 90 and reads 'Too many attempts. Try again in 90 seconds.'; registration and password-reset request at 5 per 3600 s give ceil(3600/5) = 720, the header reads Retry-After: 720 and the message is 'Too many attempts. Try again in 12 minutes.', rendered as minutes because 720 is at or above the 120-second threshold; each of those five is asserted as its own test against its own bucket; rg -nP 'Try again in \d' backend/app frontend/src returns 0 hits, every sentence interpolating the number from the refusing bucket rather than carrying a literal; rg -nP 'Try again in 900|900 seconds|900 minutes' backend/app frontend/src returns 0 hits, so the window value cannot reach a customer-facing sentence; the header is always integer seconds, asserted by rg -nP 'Retry-After.*[a-zA-Z]' over captured responses returning 0 hits, and for the 720-second case the rendered sentence is exactly 'Too many attempts. Try again in 12 minutes.' and contains no occurrence of 720, asserted over the rendered text, so the header value itself never reaches a customer and the unit word is S7.20's rather than the header's.
SourceRef: P-XCT-07 P-XCT-06 FR-ADR-058 E8 S7.4 E8 S7.20 E8 S7.21

Title: Obtain the proof's fifty sessions in an untimed warm-up so the login bucket never touches the measured window
Description: Fifty sign-ins from the script's one address exceed RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_IP_PER_15MIN at its default of 30, so without the phase split the one gate this project calls never-waivable could not obtain its sessions. A warm-up removes the login bucket from the measured result without disabling anything.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/stress_seats.py prints RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_IP_PER_15MIN and RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN, read from the environment under test, before the warm-up starts, and exits non-zero naming the missing one if it cannot read either - a run that cannot say what it ran against is not evidence; the warm-up signs fifty seeded customers in through POST /api/auth/login with no test hook, no injected token and no bypass, asserted by rg -in 'TESTING|BYPASS|X-Test|skip_auth|mint_token' scripts/stress_seats.py backend/app returning 0 hits, and holds their session cookies in memory; a warm-up sign-in refused with 429 waits its Retry-After and retries that same customer rather than failing or skipping it, so at the unchanged default of 30 the warm-up completes with a printed warmup_elapsed_seconds between 570 and 660 - 30 immediate, then 20 at one token per 30 s - and exits non-zero outside that band; the measured window issues zero requests to /api/auth/login and exactly fifty to POST /api/showtimes/41/holds, asserted by counting the API's request log lines by route for the window; any 429 inside the measured window makes the run void and the script exits non-zero printing the literal line RUN VOID: 429 inside the measured window, because a 429 there means the run measured the limiter instead of the lock; the script sets no RATE_LIMIT_ variable and passes no disabling flag, asserted by the rg -n 'RATE_LIMIT' check S-XCT-01 states.
SourceRef: P-XCT-07 P-XCT-01 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 E8 S7.1

Title: Re-run the concurrency proof at the close of Phase 7 against the live rate limiter
Description: The proof is Phase 4 and the limiter is Phase 7, so the Phase 4 run happens before the limiter exists and its condition that the limiter is not disabled is vacuous exactly when the proof first runs. The contradiction is resolved by re-running rather than by weakening either phase. A red gate at either stage marks this story Blocked with a note and is surfaced; that is governance and lives in S-XCT-41, and what is asserted here is only that the script exits non-zero.
AcceptanceCriteria: At the close of Phase 7, with the rate limiter present and enabled, Stage A is re-run and reports exactly 1 HTTP 201, exactly 49 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, a start-instant spread under STRESS_CONCURRENCY_SPREAD_MS and exactly 1 row from SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312; the run reports limiter_enabled = true, read from the running application's /metrics or its logged configuration line rather than assumed, and exits non-zero when it is false, because that is exactly the condition the Phase 4 run could not check; Stage B is re-run and produces exactly 1 row with the constraint present, exactly 2 with it dropped and exactly 1 with it restored, the restore read back from SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returning one row whose definition is UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id); the Phase 4 result is recorded as covering the Phase 4 configuration only, asserted by both runs' JSON outcome lines carrying distinct run_at values and distinct limiter_enabled values; both runs print the operator and run_at fields S-XCT-01 specifies and exit non-zero when STRESS_OPERATOR is unset; a red gate at either stage makes the script exit non-zero and is never faked, skipped or marked expected-to-fail, asserted by rg -n 'xfail|pytest.mark.skip' backend/tests returning 0 hits.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 P-XCT-07 P-XCT-27 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 E8 S7.18

Title: Cache the seat map and the listings cache-aside, invalidating with DEL after commit
Description: Invalidation is a DEL issued after the transaction commits and after the Redis locks are released, never a SET of the new value. The listings are the stated exception and are made unreachable by a generation value because their key set is caller-chosen and unbounded, which is the same idea rather than a relaxation; that mechanism is P-BRW-12's and is not restated here.
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat map is cached at cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} with SEATMAP_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (10) and the listings at their own key with LISTING_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (60), asserted by reading TTL cache:seatmap:41 immediately after a miss and finding a value between 1 and 10 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; after a hold, a release or a booking commits, EXISTS cache:seatmap:41 returns 0 immediately after the response - the entry is deleted and never replaced with a computed value, which is what distinguishes a DEL from a SET; a recording Redis client asserts the command order for one hold is SET lock:seat:41:312 NX, then the transaction COMMIT, then DEL of the lock key, then DEL cache:seatmap:41, in that order and no other; a rebuild acquires cache:seatmap:41:rebuild with SET NX PX CACHE_REBUILD_LOCK_TTL_MS (default 2000, read from configuration and asserted by rg -n '2000' backend/app/core/cache.py returning 0 hits), and a caller that does not get the lock waits for at most CACHE_REBUILD_LOCK_TTL_MS, re-reads the cache, and on a second miss reads PostgreSQL directly rather than blocking, asserted by two concurrent misses both returning 200 whose seats arrays are equal element for element and in the same order - the comparison is on the seat states and not on the whole body, which may carry a per-response generated instant - and exactly one of them issuing the rebuild query; a DEL that raises is neither retried nor rolled back, asserted by patching it to raise and observing the booking still committed and the entry gone within 10 s; rg -F 'stampede' backend/app/core/cache.py returns at least one hit, so the site carries the comment naming the scenario; worst-case staleness a customer can see is 10 s cache TTL plus 3 s poll interval = 13 s, asserted against real Redis in real elapsed time rather than against the injected clock, because Redis expires its own keys on its own clock and advancing the application's clock leaves the cache entry in place: a seat is released and a poll reports it available no more than 13 s of real elapsed time after the release; a stale map never causes an oversell, which S-XCT-01's gate asserts.

Title: Behave differently for each of Redis's three jobs when Redis is gone
Description: Locks fail loudly, the cache degrades to PostgreSQL, the limiter fails closed, and readiness still returns 503. The limiter runs before the cache, so the rate-limited seat-map read returns 503 rather than 200 from PostgreSQL - the stricter of two APPROVED records, adopted without a signature.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the Redis container stopped: POST /api/showtimes/41/holds and POST /api/bookings each return 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE on the configured client timeout with message 'Seat holds are unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.'; GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes return 200 served from PostgreSQL, because they are not rate-limited; GET /api/showtimes/41/seatmap returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and not 200, because it is rate-limited, the limiter runs before the cache and it fails closed, and its message is exactly 'The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.' (P-BRW-12, which owns that code on that endpoint) and no variant of it; every other limited endpoint returns 503 with message 'That is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.'; GET /health/ready returns 503 with body checks.redis = 'unreachable' within READINESS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3 s); the Redis client carries explicit connect and command timeouts read from named configuration variables, asserted by rg -n 'socket_connect_timeout|socket_timeout' backend/app/core/redis.py returning both, so an unreachable node produces a 503 rather than a hung request; the hold path issues zero SQL statements while Redis is unreachable, asserted by a statement-counting SQLAlchemy listener, and rg -n 'FOR UPDATE|advisory_lock|pg_advisory' backend/app/domain/holds.py returns 0 hits, so there is no PostgreSQL fallback for locking; after a Redis restart every live hold is gone and the next confirm on one of them returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with message 'The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged. Choose them again if they are still free.' (P-HLD-14 row 5).

Title: Serve /health/live and /health/ready with deliberately different behaviour
Description: A liveness check that touches a dependency turns every dependency outage into a restart loop; a readiness check that does not touch one keeps a broken instance in the load balancer. Collapsing the two defeats why they exist. Which endpoint goes where is Zone C and the client wires it.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /health/live returns 200 with body {"status": "live"} while the process can serve HTTP, and issues no database query, no Redis command, no disk read and no network call - asserted by stopping both PostgreSQL and Redis and still receiving 200, and by a counting SQLAlchemy listener and a counting Redis client wrapper each recording 0 calls for the request; GET /health/ready runs SELECT 1 against PostgreSQL and PING against Redis on a short timeout and returns 200 with {"status": "ready", "checks": {"postgres": "ok", "redis": "ok"}, "payment_provider": <PAYMENT_PROVIDER>}; with PostgreSQL stopped it returns 503 with checks.postgres not equal to 'ok' while /health/live still returns 200; with Redis stopped, 503 naming redis; with both stopped, 503 naming both; with SES, SQS or S3 unavailable it still returns 200, asserted by pointing each at an unroutable endpoint in turn; with PostgreSQL's port blackholed rather than refused, /health/ready returns 503 in under 2 seconds while the test client's own timeout is set to 10 seconds, so the 503 is the server's own timeout and not the caller's; a second request within READINESS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3) issues no further SELECT 1 or PING, asserted by the same counting wrappers; neither endpoint requires a session, asserted by calling both with no cookie and receiving 200, and neither body carries a version, a hostname or a connection string, asserted by matching each body against the regex (version|hostname|postgres://|redis://) and finding no match, PAYMENT_PROVIDER being the one deliberate disclosure; rg -n 'restart loop' backend/app/api/health.py returns at least one hit, the comment on /health/live saying what breaks if it is made to touch a dependency; rg -F '/health/ready' 'docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md' returns at least one hit on the load balancer row, and rg -F 'reversing them turns a recoverable outage into a restart loop' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit.
SourceRef: P-XCT-10 SRC-002 §7.4 FR-ADR-055 FR-ADR-041 E8 S7.7 EP-XCT-01 EP-XCT-02

Title: Return one error envelope with a stable code, and show a request id on 5xx only
Description: The interface branches on code, never on message - branching on 409 alone produces one screen for five situations. The framework's own validation error shape is replaced, because a default 422 body would break the contract on exactly the errors a form hits most.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every error response, including the framework's own validation failure and its own method-not-allowed, is the envelope {"error": {"code", "message", "details", "request_id"}}, asserted by a test that forces one failure on every mounted route and validates each captured body against that JSON schema with no additional top-level properties; the interface branches on code, asserted by rg -nP '\.message\s*===|\.message\s*==|message\.includes\(' frontend/src returning 0 hits; an unhandled exception returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with message 'The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote {request_id}.' and the stack trace in the log only; a body that fails validation returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the failing field names in details; a path or resource that does not exist for any method returns 404 NOT_FOUND with message 'That page does not exist.'; a unique-constraint violation on seat occupancy returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and never INTERNAL_ERROR, because it is the guard working; a 4xx carries request_id in the body and the rendered page does not display it, while a 5xx page's rendered text contains the eight-character id; no captured body from the forced-failure sweep matches the regex (Traceback|File \"|SELECT |INSERT |psycopg|sqlalchemy|booking_seat|\.rds\.amazonaws\.com); the five 409 codes SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, HOLD_EXPIRED, SALES_CLOSED, IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT and VERSION_CONFLICT each drive a different interface branch, asserted by five separate interface tests each asserting a different rendered string. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.

Title: Answer a method no route serves with 405 in the product envelope, from one global handler
Description: A route mounted only to say no is a route somebody will later make work, so the never-deleted entities get no DELETE route at all and a global handler renders the envelope instead. The message is generic and entity-blind by necessity: routing failed before any handler ran, and a sentence naming the entity would be a claim the code cannot support.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /health/live returns HTTP 405 carrying the product envelope with code METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and message 'That action is not available. Nothing was changed.', rendered by one exception handler mounted on the application and on no router, asserted by rg -c 'method_not_allowed' backend/app returning exactly one handler registration; a DELETE addressed at /api/admin/movies/{id}, /api/admin/showtimes/{id}, /api/admin/screens/{id}, /api/admin/cinemas/{id} and each of the four lookup vocabulary paths returns the same 405 with the same body, and walking the mounted route table finds no DELETE route on any of those paths; DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} is a real mounted route that returns 204 while its hall has no showtime rows at all, and never reaches this handler; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE addressed at /api/reports/dashboard each return the same 405, because that path exists and serves GET; GET /api/nothing-here returns 404 NOT_FOUND and not 405, so 'no such address' and 'not that verb' stay separable; rg -F 'METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED' 'docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json' returns 1 hit - the merge owner added METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED to VALID_CODES and the contract on 2026-08-22, so the code IS present and a criterion asserting its absence is stale to VALID_CODES in docs/03 PRD/api/generate_api.py, a lane finding it ABSENT would be reading a stale contract and must re-generate before concluding anything.
SourceRef: P-XCT-11 P-XCT-05 FR-ADR-052 FR-ADR-012 E8 S6

Title: Emit JSON logs to stdout with a request id we generate
Description: One object per line to stdout, never a file. An inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted for correlation. Eight lowercase hex characters is a length chosen so a person can read it aloud or type it from a screen, and it is a correlation aid rather than a key - about a half chance of a collision by 77,000 ids, stated rather than glossed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every log line is one JSON object on stdout carrying timestamp, level, logger, message, service, instance_id and request_id, asserted by capturing stdout for a full test run and parsing every line with json.loads and checking the seven keys; rg -n 'FileHandler|RotatingFileHandler|WatchedFileHandler' backend/app backend/migrations returns 0 hits and rg -nP "open\(.*\.log" backend/app backend/migrations returns 0 hits; the request id is generated per request from secrets and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ - eight lowercase hexadecimal characters, which is what {request_id} in every published string is; a request carrying X-Request-Id: injected-by-caller is logged with client_request_id 'injected-by-caller' and a request_id that still matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ and differs from it; every response carries the generated id in the X-Request-Id header, asserted on a 200, a 404 and a 500; exactly one INFO line is written per completed request carrying route, method, status_code and duration_ms, asserted by counting lines whose message field is 'request completed' for one request and finding 1; a SEAT_UNAVAILABLE outcome produces a line at level INFO and no line at level WARNING, and increments seat_conflicts_total; two GET /health/live requests produce no INFO line while a /health/ready failure produces one at WARNING or above; SELECT count(*) FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexdef LIKE '%request_id%' AND indexdef LIKE 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX%' returns 0 and rg -nP 'JOIN[^;]*request_id' backend/app returns 0 hits. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.

Title: Propagate the request id from the confirm into the worker's receipt job
Description: Without the propagation the worker's line is unfindable from the API's, and 'what happened to this booking' cannot be answered end to end from one search. The consequence that makes the whole logging specification worth having is Zone C: container stdout dies with the container unless the awslogs driver is configured, which the prep queue carries with a needed-by of Phase 1.
AcceptanceCriteria: The booking's outbox row carries the originating request_id in a request_id column, it travels in the queue message payload, and it is bound to the worker's logging context for the whole job, asserted by SELECT request_id FROM outbox WHERE booking_id = 9008 returning {request_id} and by the received message body's JSON carrying the same value; filtering the captured stdout of the API and the worker for the literal string {request_id} returns both the API line, whose parsed JSON carries service 'api', route '/api/bookings', status_code 201 and booking_id 9008, and the worker line, whose parsed JSON carries service 'worker', a non-null job_id, booking_id 9008 and message 'receipt sent', asserted end to end in an integration test that runs the API and the worker against one ElasticMQ queue; the migrate command's stdout lines each parse as JSON and carry service 'migrate', so the migration run logs the same way as the API and the worker; docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md contains a row whose Item cell contains the literal string awslogs and whose Needed by cell reads Phase 1, and rg -F 'the record of a crash loop is destroyed by the restart that caused it' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit. REQUEST ID: every {request_id} above is read from this response's error.request_id (or the X-Request-Id header) at assertion time and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$; it is never compared to a literal, because the envelope generates a fresh id on every error and an inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted.

Title: Redact centrally, and never log a credential or a reference beside an email address
Description: A denylist applied on the logging pipeline rather than at the call site, because a redaction that has to be remembered at each call site is a redaction that is forgotten at one. No card data exists in this system and the rule stays stated so nobody adds a card-shaped log field out of habit.
AcceptanceCriteria: A redaction filter is installed on the logging pipeline and applies a denylist of field names centrally, asserted by a test that calls the ordinary logger with a structure containing the keys password, password_hash, jwt, authorization and cookie, changes no call site, and finds every one of the five values replaced by the literal [REDACTED] in the emitted line; over the captured stdout of a full test run, no line contains the seeded password value, no line matches the regex \$2[aby]\$\d\d\$ (a bcrypt hash), no line matches eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,} (a JWT), no line contains the literal Authorization: Bearer, and no line matches a 13-to-19-digit run (card-shaped data, which this system holds none of); no captured line matches both [23456789ACDEFHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{8} and an @ sign, because a booking reference beside the customer's email address is enough to walk into a hall, asserted specifically over the receipt and booking log paths; LOG_LEVEL's declared default in backend/app/core/config.py is INFO and rg -nP 'ENVIRONMENT|APP_ENV' backend/app/core/logging.py returns 0 hits, so no code path raises or lowers it by environment, and rg -F 'LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, the runbook being where it is refused.
SourceRef: P-XCT-12 SRC-002 §7.6 FR-ADR-056 E8 S7.8

Title: Expose /metrics in Prometheus format, and record in writing that nothing scrapes it
Description: Built because SRC-002 §7.7 requires it and because it is a learning deliverable. Nothing in the approved stack scrapes it, nothing stores its history and nothing alerts on it, and that is said plainly rather than absorbed. Adding Prometheus, Grafana Cloud or a CloudWatch Prometheus scrape needs the client's permission first and is not designed around.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /metrics on the container's port returns Prometheus text exposition format with Content-Type 'text/plain; version=0.0.4' and the parsed body carries all eight series - http_requests_total{route,method,status}, http_request_duration_seconds{route}, seat_locks_held, queue_depth, seat_conflicts_total, booking_confirmations_total{outcome}, receipt_dispatch_total{outcome} and outbox_pending - asserted by name against a list of exactly eight and failing on a ninth; the API runs a single uvicorn worker per container, asserted by rg -n 'workers' over the entrypoint returning either no hit or the literal 1, so a scrape returns the whole process's counters; the worker serves its own /metrics on WORKER_METRICS_PORT (default 8001), which differs from API_PORT (default 8000) and makes the process exit non-zero at boot when equal to it or outside 1024-65535; a scrape issues exactly one Redis command, asserted by a counting client wrapper, and rg -n 'scan_iter|SCAN' backend/app/api/metrics.py returns 0 hits, so seat_locks_held is read from an O(1) counter and never by a SCAN per scrape, its drift being reconciled by a bounded SCAN on the worker's existing receive loop and not on a schedule; two scrapes one second apart issue exactly one SQS GetQueueAttributes call, asserted by a counting stub, and with SQS unroutable the second scrape still returns 200 with queue_depth carrying its last value and a queue_depth_age_seconds series beside it; rg -F '/metrics' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit and rg -F 'No load balancer listener rule may match /metrics' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit; rg -F 'Nothing scrapes this endpoint, nothing stores its history and nothing alerts on it.' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit.

Description: Validation runs at import time, before the application accepts a request. A container that starts and then fails on its first booking is worse than one that never starts, because the container runtime reports it healthy. A sensible default so the app starts locally is forbidden for exactly that reason.
AcceptanceCriteria: With DATABASE_URL unset the process exits non-zero printing a message containing the literal DATABASE_URL and never binds its port, and the same holds one at a time for REDIS_URL, QUEUE_URL, JWT_SECRET and COOKIE_SECURE, none of which has a default, asserted by rg -n 'Field\(' backend/app/core/config.py showing no default for any of the five; API_PORT and WORKER_METRICS_PORT set equal, and each set to 80 and to 70000, exit non-zero in both the api and the worker process; the resolved configuration is logged exactly once at boot, asserted by counting lines whose message is 'configuration resolved' and finding 1, with every value whose name matches (SECRET|PASSWORD|TOKEN|URL) rendered as [REDACTED] and PAYMENT_PROVIDER present; rg -nP 'ENVIRONMENT|APP_ENV|is_prod|if .*production' backend/app returns 0 hits; the set of variable names declared in the settings model equals the set of names in .env.example, asserted by a test comparing the two sets and printing the difference; Title: Read secrets from SSM through the task definition and never from the application
Description: The application reads an ordinary environment variable and knows nothing about SSM - no SDK call for configuration, no client, no bootstrap fetch, no IAM dependency at read time. AWS Secrets Manager is forbidden. Locally the same variables come from a .env file so the code path is identical in both environments. The working practice of scanning the staged diff before every push is a habit rather than a check; what is asserted is the state of the repository, which is where a leaked credential would show.
AcceptanceCriteria: rg -in 'ssm|get_parameter|parameter_store' backend/app returns 0 hits and rg -no "boto3.client\(['\"][a-z0-9]+" backend/app returns only s3, sqs and ses - the application reads JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL as ordinary environment variables; git check-ignore .env exits 0; rg -nP '(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|xox[baprs]-)' . returns 0 hits - this one scan stays over the whole repository, documentation trees included and deliberately not narrowed, because a credential pasted into a document is still a committed credential, and it is safe at the root because each of the three alternatives is written with a character class or a quantifier and none matches its own text, which is itself checked by running the same command against docs/05 Bible/ and finding 0 hits - so no credential is committed and no decrypted SecureString value has been written into a log or a document; the build session creates no parameter, no role and no task definition, asserted by rg -nP 'aws ssm (put-parameter|delete-parameter)|aws iam (create|attach|put)|register-task-definition' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src scripts/ docker-compose.yml returning 0 hits, scoped away from the repository root because this criterion quotes the command strings it searches for and a root-wide run matches its own text in docs/05 Bible/;
