Title: Drain on SIGTERM and release this instance's holds through a Redis registry
Description: The registry is a set in Redis and not process memory: statelessness forbids local state, and a process SIGKILLed after the grace period loses in-memory state before it can act on it. Correctness never depends on the release running - the locks expire in three minutes - which is the property that makes this safe to get wrong. The lock-release half has nothing to release until Phase 4 and is re-checked there.
AcceptanceCriteria: On SIGTERM the API stops accepting new connections, waits out the deregistration delay so in-flight requests already routed complete, finishes them bounded by SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (20), reads SMEMBERS instance:{instance_id}:holds and runs the compare-and-delete release for each key, then exits - asserted by sending SIGTERM to a running container mid-request and observing that request complete with its normal 201 and EXISTS lock:seat:41:312 return 0 afterwards; each API instance generates its id at boot and adds each granted hold's keys to its own registry set with the same 180-second TTL as the holds, asserted by TTL instance:{instance_id}:holds returning a value between 1 and 180 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; the registry lives in Redis and not in process memory, asserted by SIGKILLing the container and reading SMEMBERS instance:{old_instance_id}:holds from a second container, which still returns the key; a key whose token no longer matches is a no-op and cannot free another customer's lock, asserted by expiring a hold, re-acquiring it as a second customer, then draining the first instance and observing GET lock:seat:41:312 still return the second customer's token; with the release skipped entirely the seats are unbuyable for at most 180 s, asserted by TTL, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking is unchanged; on SIGTERM the worker stops polling, finishes the message it is handling, completes any outbox relay batch in progress and exits with status 0, asserted by SIGTERM mid-job and observing SELECT status FROM receipt_dispatch for that job reach a terminal value; rg -F 'the ECS stop timeout must exceed the deregistration delay plus SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, and the same file contains the literal string 'SIGKILL arriving during the drain skips the release'.

Title: Keep every container stateless
Description: Killing any container mid-request must not corrupt data. A file is state on a stateless container and dies with it; a rate-limit counter in process memory multiplies its own limit by the number of processes while appearing to work. Both images declare a read-only root filesystem as their intended runtime mode and enforcing it is Zone C.
AcceptanceCriteria: Both images run with a read-only root filesystem and serve requests without error, asserted by starting the compose stack with read_only: true on the api and worker services and running both test suites against it; logs go to stdout and no file is written to local disk, asserted by docker diff on each container after a full suite returning no line beginning with A or C outside /tmp and /var/run; a poster upload streams to the object store and never touches the container's disk, asserted by the same docker diff after an upload; the guest's seat selection across the sign-in round trip is readable from the browser's sessionStorage key fr.pending_selection - the one-shot key owned by P-ACC-13, the per-change key fr.selection being E2's - asserted by reading it back and finding its parsed seat ids are exactly C12 and C13, and no server-side row and no Redis key holds it, asserted by SELECT count(*) over every table in the public schema being unchanged across the round trip and by a full SCAN COUNT 1000 of the Redis keyspace before the sign-in and after the return producing the identical key set, with SCAN MATCH '*selection*' returning zero keys at both points; the per-instance hold registry and the rate-limit counters both live in Redis, asserted by SIGKILLing the API container, starting a new one, and finding the user's rate-limit bucket count unchanged and SMEMBERS instance:{old_id}:holds still readable; both images run as a non-root user created in the Dockerfile, asserted by docker run --entrypoint id returning a non-zero uid, and a container asked to bind port 80 exits non-zero at boot; the API listens on API_PORT (default 8000) and rg -F 'API_PORT' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, the specification naming that number for the target group, the security group ingress rule and the published port; SIGKILL sent to a running container mid-confirm leaves no partial state, asserted as a real signal test against a running stack and not as a unit test: SELECT count(*) FROM booking b LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.id = b.payment_id WHERE p.id IS NULL returns 0, SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312 returns 0 or 1, and TTL lock:seat:41:312 returns a value between 1 and 180 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all; a replacement container serves the same request with the same Idempotency-Key and returns the identical body.

Title: Run migrations as a separate explicit step and never on boot
Description: There is no code path in the API or the worker that can apply a migration - not at import, not in a lifespan hook, not in the entrypoint's default path, not behind a flag. Alembic does not take an advisory lock, which is widely believed and is not true, and removing that race is the reason for the rule.
AcceptanceCriteria: rg -in 'alembic' backend/app returns 0 hits and rg -n 'upgrade\(' backend/app returns 0 hits - no application code path can apply a migration, not at import, not in a lifespan hook, not behind a flag; the container entrypoint accepts exactly four commands, api, worker, migrate and seed, asserted by invoking it with a fifth and receiving a non-zero exit naming the four, and only migrate runs alembic upgrade head and exits with the migration's status, while api and worker start a long-running process and issue no alembic command, asserted by rg -n 'alembic' over the entrypoint returning hits only inside the migrate branch; starting the image with api against a database one revision behind starts the process, returns 200 from /health/live and /health/ready, and returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR at the first request touching a new column rather than failing at boot, and rg -F 'starts healthy and fails at the first query touching a new column' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit so the runbook names that symptom; every revision file's downgrade body is a single raise NotImplementedError, asserted by a test parsing each file under backend/migrations/versions with ast and finding the downgrade function's body is exactly one Raise node; every revision file matching rg -l 'audit_log|booking_seat' backend/migrations/versions also matches rg -l '# LOCK:' backend/migrations/versions - both scans carry that path, because an rg with no path argument runs from the repository root and this criterion quotes the marker it searches for - the comment naming what is locked and for roughly how long; rg -n 'drop_column|drop_table|alter_column' backend/migrations/versions returns 0 hits, so no revision can break the old code that runs against the new schema during the deploy window; SELECT rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user returns false when connected with the local compose stack's DATABASE_URL; rg -F '1 manual snapshot, 2 one-off migrate task, 3 verify the task exited 0, 4 update the service' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit and the same file contains the literal strings 'reversing 2 and 4 runs new code against an old schema' and 'skipping 1 makes 2 unrecoverable after seven days'.

Title: Specify the backup, and rehearse the restore with a recorded outcome
Description: A restore that has never been rehearsed is not a recovery. Enabling backups, setting the window and running a restore are all AWS commands that create or modify infrastructure, so they are Zone C and the build session performs none of them. Needed by Phase 2 - the first phase that creates data worth losing - and announced now rather than on the day it blocks.
AcceptanceCriteria: docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md contains a row whose Item cell contains the literal string 'RDS automated backups' and whose Needed by cell reads Phase 2; the Zone C specification that row's Spec cell names exists under docs/30 Deployment/ and contains the literal strings 'retention 7 days', 'point-in-time recovery', 'a backup window outside the cinema's busy period' and 'a manual snapshot before every migration'; the same file contains the literal strings 'a restore creates a new RDS instance with a new endpoint', 'deleting an instance without a final snapshot deletes its automated backups with it', 'a corruption discovered in week three is not recoverable from an automated backup' and 'forever retention and a 7-day backup window are different guarantees'; it contains the literal strings 'Redis is not backed up: it holds locks and cache' and 'S3 posters are not backed up: nothing deletes a poster and a new poster is a new key'; the Phase 7 rehearsal restores to a new instance, points a local application at it by changing DATABASE_URL alone, and confirms a known seeded booking is present and correct - reference K7M2QX9B, rendered FR-K7M2-QX9B, seats C12 and C13, both Premium at 28124 paise each (the seeded base of 24999 at the 1250-basis-point Premium uplift), so the total is exactly 2 * 28124 = 56248 paise - read back with SELECT b.reference, s.row_label, s.seat_number, bs.price_paise FROM booking b JOIN booking_seat bs ON bs.booking_id = b.id JOIN seat s ON s.id = bs.seat_id WHERE b.reference = 'K7M2QX9B'; the rehearsal writes one JSON line carrying operator (read from RESTORE_OPERATOR, which has no default, the run exiting non-zero and naming RESTORE_OPERATOR when it is unset), run_at, restored_instance and the three values read back, because an undated claim that it was run is not evidence.
SourceRef: P-XCT-20 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02 SRC-002 §5.2.2 FR-ADR-070 E8 S7.15

Title: Fit three processes inside roughly 1 GB, with explicit limits and measured replacement
Description: Three long-running processes, not four - the scheduler is deleted and there is nothing left for it to run. Say it rather than work around it is the binding rule: a measured figure over its limit is reported with the number and what it would take to fit.
AcceptanceCriteria: Exactly three long-running application processes exist and no fourth, asserted by parsing docker-compose.yml and finding its services are exactly api, worker, web, postgres, redis and elasticmq, of which api, worker and web are the application's and web serves static files rather than running Node, asserted by rg -n 'node|npm start|vite preview' over the web service's Dockerfile final stage returning 0 hits; the API runs one uvicorn worker per container and the database pool size is set from named configuration rather than defaulted, asserted by rg -n 'pool_size|max_overflow' backend/app/core/db.py returning both sourced from settings, and the specification states the arithmetic against roughly 110 maximum connections on db.t3.micro multiplied across processes; rg -c '^FROM ' backend/Dockerfile and the frontend/src Dockerfile each return 2 or more, and docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' on the final backend/app backend/migrations image returns a value under 262144000 bytes (250 MB), against ECR's 500 MB free tier, with the figure written into the specification; at the close of Phase 1 the resident set size of each container is measured at idle and under load with docker stats and every row of the budget table in the specification carries the literal suffix (measured) and no row carries the literal (reasoned, not observed), replacing API ~200 MB, worker ~150 MB, static frontend/src ~15 MB, budgeted ~365 MB against 624-724 MB available after 300-400 MB for the operating system, Docker daemon and ECS agent; a measured figure over its container's limit is reported rather than worked around, asserted by that same specification file carrying one line per over-limit container naming the container, the measured figure in MB, the limit in MB and what it would take to fit, and by it carrying no such line when every measured row is inside its limit.

Title: Introduce no scheduled job of any kind
Description: A design constraint and not merely an absence: no later design may introduce one. Each place a periodic job would otherwise be reached for has a named replacement, and anything that would otherwise be 'the nightly job will fix it' has to be correct when it is written, which is stricter and deliberate.
AcceptanceCriteria: The repository contains no scheduler process, no cron container, no EventBridge rule, no Lambda on a timer and no periodic task inside a process, asserted two ways: parsing docker-compose.yml returns exactly the six services api, worker, web, postgres, redis and elasticmq and no cron or scheduler service, and rg -in 'cron|apscheduler|celery|schedule\(|eventbridge|BackgroundScheduler|repeat_every' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src docker-compose.yml returns hits only on lines that also contain the literal 'no scheduled job'; an abandoned hold becomes available with no process running - with SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS set to 2 for this test and against real Redis, measured in real elapsed time and never with the injected clock, because Redis expires its own keys on its own clock and advancing the application's clock leaves the key in place: 3 s after the hold, TTL lock:seat:41:312 returns -2 and GET /api/showtimes/41/seatmap reports seat 312 as available, with no cleanup job executed, asserted by the worker's job counter being unchanged; idempotency records are never expired, asserted by rg -in 'DELETE FROM idempotency|EXPIRE idempotency' backend/app backend/migrations returning 0 hits, because a key that expires is a key whose later retry creates a second booking; rg -in 'DELETE FROM' backend/app returns hits only on the seat delete and the manager screen assignment replace of S-XCT-09, so nothing is pruned; stuck outbox rows are relayed by the worker's existing receive loop, asserted by a test that inserts a pending outbox row older than OUTBOX_STALE_SECONDS and observes the next poll relay it with no timer involved, and the seat_locks_held counter is reconciled by a bounded SCAN on that same loop, asserted by rg -n 'scan' backend/app/workers returning hits only inside the receive loop; a stale cache entry is removed by its own TTL, asserted by TTL cache:seatmap:41 returning a value between 1 and 10 inclusive - never -1 or -2, which Redis returns for a key with no expiry and for a key that does not exist, and which would let a build that never creates the key pass at all and, 11 s of real elapsed time later against real Redis, EXISTS cache:seatmap:41 returning 0 with a recording Redis client having captured no DEL for that key.
SourceRef: P-XCT-22 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 SRC-002 §E E-4 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-012

Title: Add no service or dependency outside the approved list
Description: The stack is fixed by SRC-002 §4 and anything outside it needs the client's permission first. Permission has been sought and granted exactly twice - Amazon SES, now on the approved list, and ElasticMQ for local development only. A dependency that is not obviously necessary costs the client a decision, and there is only one decider. Any further addition is put to the client with what it buys and what it costs before it enters the design, and the answer is recorded; that is a governance rule and not a runnable check, so what is asserted below is the state of the two manifests and the deployment specification.
AcceptanceCriteria: backend/requirements.txt contains no task-queue library and no Argon2 package, asserted by rg -inP '^(rq|dramatiq|celery|huey|argon2|argon2-cffi|passlib\[argon2\])\b' backend/requirements.txt returning 0 hits; frontend/package.json declares no component library, no CSS framework and no CSS-in-JS runtime, asserted by a test parsing its dependencies and devDependencies and failing on any of @mui, @chakra-ui, antd, bootstrap, react-bootstrap, tailwindcss, styled-components, @emotion; every remaining package in both manifests is compared against the recorded allowlist in the same test, which fails naming any package on neither list; rg -in 'eks|fargate|nat gateway|secretsmanager|secrets manager|managed grafana|opensearch|cloudfront|bastion|vpc interface endpoint' backend/app backend/migrations frontend/src 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns hits only on lines that also contain the literal forbidden; rg -in 'minio|mailhog' docker-compose.yml returns 0 hits and rg -F 'local development does not fully exercise the poster upload path without AWS credentials and does not exercise SES at all' 'docs/30 Deployment/' returns at least one hit, so the resulting gap is stated rather than papered over; the services the deployment specification names are exactly ECS on EC2, an Application Load Balancer, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, SQS, SES, S3, SSM Parameter Store, ECR and CloudWatch Logs, asserted against the Zone C specification file named in the Spec cell of the docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md row whose Item cell contains the literal string 'ECS cluster', which carries a Markdown list of one service per item under the heading '## Services this product uses', that list read as a set being exactly those ten.

Title: Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA as the target, compute every contrast figure, and record the one deviation
Description: Nobody asked for AA; adopting a stricter option needs no signature. Every contrast ratio is computed and recorded rather than asserted, and no conformance is claimed because a claim would need testing this project has not done. OPEN-SEAT-02 ruled out accessible-seat marking, which is a product feature about wheelchair spaces and says nothing about interface accessibility.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every colour declaration in docs/05 B DesignSystem/tokens.css carries its machine-readable annotation naming what it is and which grounds it may sit on, asserted by running contrast.py against a scratch copy with one annotation removed and observing a non-zero exit naming that token; film_index = (k + d) mod 8 over k = 0..719 in ascending (day, slot, screen) order gives every film exactly 90 showtimes, asserted by SELECT movie_id, count(*) FROM showtime GROUP BY 1 returning eight rows all reading 90; runtime_minutes = 90 + i * 10 for i = 0..7, so 90 through 160; ends_at is computed once and stored as starts_at + runtime_minutes + SEED_CHANGEOVER_MINUTES with the changeover 20, so the 21:30 slot with the 160-minute film ends at 21:30 + 180 = 00:30 the next local day and the longest occupancy of 180 minutes sits inside the 210-minute slot spacing, asserted by a SELECT finding 0 overlapping pairs on any screen; Title: Give every seeded account a password it can sign in with, without committing a credential
Description: Known and unbuilt, and it stops Phase 2 and Phase 4. AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/seed.py reads SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD from the environment, which has no default and is read by the seed and by nothing else, asserted by rg -n 'SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD' backend/app returning 0 hits, so no container refuses to boot over a value it has no use for; equal to the value on the SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD line of .env.example, the seed exits non-zero, refused by value and not by pattern; the value is hashed once at BCRYPT_COST through the same function the registration path uses and that one hash is reused across all 1 + 12 + 50 = 63 accounts, asserted by a counting wrapper recording exactly 1 call to the hash function and by SELECT count(DISTINCT password_hash) FROM users returning 1; the addresses are deterministic - admin-01@, manager-01@ through manager-12@, customer-01@ through customer-50@, all at SEED_EMAIL_DOMAIN, which defaults to demo.frontrow.invalid, reserved by RFC 2606 and guaranteed never to resolve; the seed's stdout contains the three lines admin: 1, manager: 12 and customer: 50 followed by the addresses, and no captured stdout line and no file written contains the value of SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD; Title: Specify the deployed seed run as a one-off task on its own task definition family
Description: The same shape as the migration run, deliberately, so the client learns one pattern rather than two. A separate family rather than a command override, because a secret must be in a family to be resolved from it and putting it in the shared family is exactly what the seed-only rule forbids. Two families, one image, so the code and the seed stay the same build. All of it is Zone C and the build session builds none of it; that the build session also holds no write access to anything in AWS is a fact about the credentials rather than a check that can be run without making the very call it forbids.
